MOSES THE HERMIT 
St. Moses, the hermit, was born in Alexandria. Once he reached the age of 
thirteen years, he set forth to the wilderness of the Scetis. There, he dwelt for 
twenty years in a small cell next to one of the older monks. Then, he went 
deep in the wilderness an d lived for thirty -five years in a spot having olive 
and palm trees. There, he ate according to his needs whatever would fall from 
the trees, drank from the rainwater, dressed in palm leaves, and befriended 
the wild beasts.  
His Multiple Falls and Repentances:  
Satan envied this hermit, so he appeared to him in the form of an older 
man. The older man told him that he used to live a corrupt life, but he 
repented and distributed his wealth to the poor. He lived in one of the Five 
Western Cities (Pentapolis) near Cyrenaica (Barqa), and that God revealed to 
him that the hour of his death was approaching. They walked together in the 
wilderness until they reached a grand mansion. Then, the older man told the 
hermit that after his death, that mansion would be his, if he would marry his 
daughter. Moses was deceived and thought that the older man was on the 
brink of extinction, so he accepted his offer. However, once he declared his 
acceptance, he found himself amid the wilderness, hungry and afraid. He 
could not see any mansion there, and he realized that it was a trick from the 
devil. He felt how he was so weak and offered sincere repentance.  
Once St. Moses also went to Alexandria, where the devil appeared to him

MOSES, THE CONFESSOR 
This St. Moses (Moyses) was a Roman priest of Jewish roots. He was one 
of the main members of a congregation of confessors in the time of Cyprian, 
at the start of the heresy of Novat ian.1 The rest of the confessors were: Fr. 
Maximus, the priest, the two deacons Nicostratus and Rufinus, the laymen 
Urbanus, Sidonius, Macarius, and Celerinus. According to Cyprian, they 
were the first group of confessors in the days of the persecution st irred up by 
Emperor Decius (249 -251 AD). At the time of the persecution, they wrote 
down a message to exhort the confessors in Carthage to be committed to the 
system and wrote another message to Cyprian.  
After spending about a year in prison (eleven month s and few days), St. 
Moses reposed in January 251 AD, and was counted as a confessor, and even 
as a martyr. It was said that a little while before his departure, Moses refused 
to have any contact with Novatian or the five priests who were supporting 
him and followed his views. St. Moses was considering their faith and views 
as unorthodox.  
 [A Dictionary of Christian Biography, Vol. III, p. 948] 
 [Baring-Gould: November 25] 
 
MOSES, THE RECLUSE BISHOP , ST. 
The Tribes of Saracens: 
The Arabian tribes populatin g the area of Rhinoclura in -between the 
eastern Egyptian border and the Asian shores, used to worship the stars. Then 
in the year 226 AD, these tribes embraced Christianity through the efforts of 
Origen (184-253 AD). Then, those tribes 2 joined forces toge ther and formed 
one State under the reign of a queen called Mavia. By their unity, they 
created a power block that brought fear to the Arian Emperor Valens (364 -
378 AD) and forced him to seek a peace treaty with them.  
Choosing Moses as a Bishop: 
Those Chr istian tribes having united together, they felt the need for a 
bishop to shepherd them. It happened that in those days, there was a recluse 
monk named Moses in the eastern desert, he was so beloved by those 
tribesmen that they decided to choose him to be t heir bishop. Then, when

was given by the Greeks and the Romans to the nomadic tribes in the ‘Sino-Arabian’ desert…

records.question: Who was St. Mary the Egyptian?
records.answer: St. Mary the Egyptian lived in the 4th and 5th centuries AD. Her biography was told by a priest named Zosimus. She is known for a remarkable event where she crossed a river walking on water. After this miracle, she approached the priest Zosimus, worshipped with reverence, took the Holy Sacraments, and prayed to the Lord to let her depart in peace, having seen His salvation. She asked Zosimus to come to her the following year to pray for her. When he returned at the appointed time, he found her dead, worshipping to the ground with her face toward the East and her hands motionless. Near her body, he found a written message asking him to bury her and pray for her. It is believed that she reposed in the year 421 AD. Her life has been a great motivator for many to expand their spiritual strive. The Coptic Church celebrates her feast on the 16th of Baramouda every year [2].

Sinful Woman” (Luke 7:37 -50), whose name was not mentioned, Mary of 
Bethany, the sister of Martha (Luke 10:38 -42) and Mary Magdalene. 
According to the Eastern Tradition, they were considered to be three different 
persons, whereas according to the Western Tradition 1, the three of them are 
considered to be one person (the sinful woman, Mary, the sister of Martha, 
and Mary Magdalene). However, St. Ambrose (374 -397 AD) was on the 
opinion th at this issue should be left unanswered. In any case, the Western 
Tradition views St. Mary Magdalene as a fantastic role model for the 
repentant person. Since 1969, the Eastern tradition has been taken into 
consideration in the New Western Roman calendar. St. Mary Magdalene is 
celebrated by the Western Church on the 22nd of July.  
 [The Penguin Dictionary of Saints, p. 230] 
 
MARY, THE ARMENIAN (The martyr) 
A Brave Captive gets martyred: 
This St. Mary was a captive of a Muslim man, one of the soldiers of the  
Mamluk Sultan of Egypt Al-Zahir Rukn al-Din Baibars (1260-1277 AD). Her 
master tried to persuade her to deny her faith in the Lord Christ. But, she 
refused to go along and proclaimed that she was a true Christian. The man 
viciously tortured her in his hou se while she held fast to her faith. When the 
man got tired of tormenting her without any results, he finally reported her to 
the Sultan using falsehood, saying, “I have a Muslim maidservant who claims 
to be a Christian.” The Sultan brought her before him and asked her to 
declare her Islam, which she refrained to do and persisted on confessing her 
Christian faith. The Sultan ordered his men to burn her alive. They dug a 
large pit at the gate of Zoweila in Cairo, where a great multitude came to 
watch. Then, they brought Mary to the edge of the fiery pit to scare her up 
and force her to change her mind. However, the saint bravely shouted : “It is 
great for me, O Sultan, to deliver my soul into the hands of my Lord God and 
Savior Jesus Christ.” Then, she quickly jumped into fire, where she received 
the crown of martyrdom. 
 [The Synaxarion: 27 Mesra] 
 
MARY, THE EGYPTIAN, ST. 
St. Mary, the Egyptian lived in the 4 th and 5 th centuries AD, and her 
biography was told by a priest called Zosimus, who lived in one of the 
 
1 Proposed by the Roman Pope ‘Gregory the Great’ (590-604 AD).

and then she crossed the river walking on the water. Seeing that miracle, the 
priest Zosimus attempted to bow before her. She cried out loudly, “O Father 
priest, what are you doing? Did you forget that you are carrying the Holy 
Sacraments?” She then approached, worshipped with reverence, took the 
Holy Sacraments, then raised her hands toward heaven, crying out: “Lord, let 
your servant depart in peace, for my eyes have seen Your Salvation .” (Luke 
2:29-30) She asked him to come to her in the following year, in the same 
place, to pray for her. She made the sign of the Cross on the river, crossed it 
back walking on the water, and disappeared from his sight. 
Her Departure: 
In the following year, and in the appointed time, the priest se t forth to the 
designated place, where he found the saint worshipping to the ground, with 
her face directed toward the East, and her hands motionless. Perceiving that 
she was already dead, he worshipped beside her, cried, and prayed on her the 
funeral prayers. Up to this moment, he realized that he did not even come to 
know her name; but when he got close to her, he found a written message 
saying, “Father Zosimus! Bury here the body of the miserable Mary and 
leave to the dust this sinful body. Pray on my behalf.”  
Fr. Zosimus realized that she died the year before after she had the Holy 
Sacraments he brought for her. It is believed that she reposed in the year 421 
AD. Returning to his monastery, Fr. Zosimus kept saying to himself: “Indeed, 
the tax -collectors, the sinners and the adulterers will precede us to the 
Kingdom of Heaven.” St. ‘Mary’s life was a big motivator for so many to 
expand their spiritual strive. The Coptic Church celebrates her feast on the 
16th of Baramouda every year. 
[Fragrant Bouquets from the Biographies of the Righteous and Saints, pp. 249-253] 
[The Vita of St. Mary of Egypt written by St. Sophronius, the patriarch of 
Jerusalem (634–638 AD)] 
 
MARY, THE ISRAELITE (The martyr) 
During the early life of St. Mary, the Israelite, she did not know the Lord 
Christ, and she led a sinful life. When she wanted to repent and to return to 
the righteous life, the Lord sent to her a saintly man who preached her and 
revealed to her the way of  salvation through believing in the Lord Christ. He 
told her that the soul would have to give an answer for all her deeds on the 
Day of Resurrection. After death and departure from this world, everyone 
will be rewarded according to his deeds. The man explained to her the fearful 
punishments for the evildoers. She asked him: "What are the proofs to what 
you have said to me since the ‘Torah’ that God gave to ‘Moses the Prophet’

Gethsemane. While they were going in their way, some Jews came and tried 
to prevent them from burying her. When one of them stretched his hands to 
hold the coffin, his arms separated from his body and remained hanging until 
he believed and showed remorse on his evil deed. By the supplications of the 
saintly disciples, his arms were attached back to his body.  
It happened that Thomas the Apostle was not present at the time the Virgin 
St. Mary reposed. However, in his way back to Jerusalem, he saw her 
shrouded body being carried by the angels to be taken up to heaven; and he 
was advised by one of the angels to hasten and kiss her pure body,  which he 
did. When he arrived to join the disciples, and they told him about her 
departure, he said to them, “I shall not believe unless I see her body, for you 
already know how I doubted the resurrection of the Lord Christ.” They took 
him to her tomb and  were shocked and surprised to see it empty. However, 
Thomas, the Apostle, told them how he saw her pure body with the angels 
carrying it up to heaven. The Holy Spirit told them that God did not intend 
for her pure body to remain on earth, and the Lord Chr ist promised his pure 
disciples to let them see her in the flesh again, and they waited for this true 
promise until the 16 th of the month of Mesra when it was fulfilled. She lived 
on earth 60 years: she spent 12 years in the Temple, 30 years in the house o f 
the righteous Joseph the Carpenter, and 14 years in the house of St. John the 
Evangelist, according to the commandment of the Lord, who said to her: 
“Woman! Behold your son,” and to John: “Behold! Your mother” (John 
19:26-27). The first church, which was  built in the name of the Virgin St. 
Mary, was in the city of Philippi, in Greece. That happened after the 
preaching of St. Paul and St. Barnabas to the Gentiles in that city, and when 
many of them believed, they built that church. 
The Virgin St. Mary prov ided twice special blessings to the Land of 
Egypt. The first time when she fled to Egypt with the infant Jesus and St. 
Joseph the Carpenter, running away from king Herod who intended to kill the 
infant. the second time when she appeared in spiritual ways, inside and 
outside the domes of the church consecrated in her name in the area of El -
Zeitoun, in the suburbs of Cairo on the 2 nd of April 1968 (24 Baramhat 1684 
AM). Her appearances continued for many consecutive nights. 
The Church celebrates the Birthday of St. Mary on the 1 st of Bashons, her 
Entrance into the Temple on the 3 rd of Kiahk, her Departure on the 21 st of 
Toba, the Ascension of her body to Heaven on the 16th of Mesra, Building the 
first Church in her name on the 21 st of Paona, Consecrating the church in her 
name in the ‘Muĥarraq’ monastery, which the Lord Christ blessed by his 
presence along with His Apostles, on the 6 th of Hator and her Apparition in 
the church of El-Zeitoun on the 24th of Baramhat.

crying, and what is bothering you?” She answered him: “I wish I would have 
died two years ago.” Remembering that she disappeared two years before, 
her uncle tried to control the situation, and he ask ed the owner to bring her a 
drink. Father Ibrahim started to talk to her about God’s love for the sinners, 
the adulterers, and the repentant; and that God is always ready to forgive 
them if they forsake their evil ways. Here, Mary was trembling and kept 
crying, so he told her: “Look at me; I am your uncle Ibrahim the monk, who 
raised you. I kept searching for you everywhere , and when I saw you, I tried 
to hide my tears, lest anyone would recognize me . The Lord Christ said: 
‘Those who are well are in no need  for a physician, but those who are sick; I 
did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance’ (Mark 2:17).” 
Instantly and without letting anyone notice, the two of them creeped out of 
the house of sin, forsaking the place of iniquity.  
Back to her Old Cell: 
After those events, the nun entered into her old cell once more, crying out 
and sorrowful for what she did. From that time on, everybody passing by her 
cell used to hear the sound of her unceasing cries of repentance. In the 
meantime, her un cle St. Ibrahim, departed to the heavenly Jerusalem at 85 
years of age. The Church celebrates his departure on the 30th of Toba. 
The striving saintly nun lived for about five more years after the departure 
of her uncle, continuously weeping and sorrowfully  singing songs of praise. 
Yet, God gave her a proof of His forgiveness of her sins, by granting her the 
gift of healing the sick near the end of her life.  
Then, she fell ill for a short time and reposed in peace, with her 
countenance shining with the light of the grace of repentance. 
 [The Paradise of the Female Saints, Part 1, p. 116] 
 
MARY, THE VIRGIN CONFESSOR, ST. 
A Maidservant Testifies to the Lord Christ: 
St. Mary lived in the 4 th century, as a maidservant to a noble Roman man 
called Tertullus. Since  her childhood, she was a Christian, and she was the 
only Christian in her master’s household. She kept practicing all her prayers 
and fasting, particularly during the pagan festivals. This provoked the anger 
of her mistress, though she endured her maidservant because of her honesty. 
Delivered to the Governor: 
When the persecution of the Christians started, Tertullus vainly tried to 
force his maidservant to deny her faith. However, when he failed, he

But the Father sent a single cloud to overshadow them to assure them that the Church is one 
and includes the people of God in both Testaments, made as one in the Lord Christ. 
May the Lord grant us to walk in faith that works through love, that we may ascend by 
His Holy Spirit in to the presence of the Savior in fellowship  with the saints, so that the 
Lord may reveal to us and to all humanity the splendor of His glory in our hearts, and so 
that the world may be transformed into an icon of heaven, where love, joy, and peace reign. 
1084. What are the feasts of the Theotokos, the Mother of God? 
In addition to the monthly commemoration of the Virgin Mary on the 21 st of every 
Coptic month, we celebrate the following feasts: 
a. The annunciation of her birth (7th Mesore / 13 th August). On this feast we 
celebrate the conception of St. Mary, the living ark of the covenant, the dwelling of 
the Most High, and the second heaven. 
b. Her birthday (1st Pashons / 9th May). Copts usually commemorate the day a saint 
passed from this world; their  martyrdom or departure to paradise  — but they insist 
on honoring St. Mary on her the day of her birth as a joyful day.  
c. Her entry into the temple (3rd Kiahk / 12 th December). We learn from the 
tradition of the Church that St. Mary’s life was consecrated to God in fulfillment of 
her mother’s vow, for she had vowed to consecrate her firstborn — whether a son or 
a daughter — to serve the Lord all the days of his or her life. 
d. Her departure (21st Tobe / 29th January). 
e. The revealing of the  assumption of her body (16 th Mesore / 22nd August). This 
feast is preceded by the fifteen-day fast of St. Mary. 
f. The consecration of the first church in her name at Philippi (21st Paone / 28th 
June). This feast also coincides with the commemoration of the Virgin’s miracle of 
melting iron in the city of Bartus. 
g. The apparition of the Virgin Mary above her church in Zeitoun (24 th 
Paremhotep / 2nd April). This apparition is considered unique among the whole 
history of Marian apparitions .624 It began on 2 nd April 1968 and was repeated on 
most days  for hours  at a time and  for many months. These apparitions appeared 
above the domes of the Church of St. Mary and were seen by several hundred 
thousand people, of all ages and positions, Christians and Muslims. Every night, the 
people would gather around the church, pray , and praise God, waiting to see the 
dazzling spectacle of  St. Mary standing above one of the domes. She was seen  
kneeling before the cross , or at other times,  carrying the baby Jesus. These

wondered within themselves whether there were any others out there, who 
surpassed them spiritually to learn from them and follow their path. Among 
those Fathers were St. Anthony the Great, to whom the Lord revealed the 
existence of St. Paul the First Hermit, St. Zosima th e Priest, whom the Lord 
guided to St. Mary the Egyptian, and St. Macarius the Great,  to whom the 
Lord revealed the two married women in Alexandria, who lived by the spirit 
of love, sanctity, and asceticism. 
A Married Couple Living better than a Monk: 
Such a thought came upon one of the saintly elder monks, and a Divine 
voice informed him that there was a virtuous wife called Mary living with her 
husband Ephcharistos in a village in Egypt at a spiritual level higher than 
him. By the guidance of an angel, the elderly monk set forth to that village, to 
meet with that couple who did surpass him spiritually. Knocking at their 
door, the woman opened for him, while her husband was still away 
shepherding a flock of sheep. In the evening, Ephcharistos came home and 
joined in welcoming their guest. After they prepared dinner for him, the 
monk refused ultimately to eat until they would tell him about what was 
going on in their lives. Ephcharistos did not want to talk about their private 
life together. He just said: “I a m a shepherd, and this is Mary, my wife.” The 
elder monk persisted on knowing more about them and revealed to the man 
that it was God who sent him to them. Here, the man started talking with the 
fear of the Lord. He said: “I shepherd the sheep we inherited  from our 
parents, and whenever we make a little profit by the help of God, we divide it 
into three portions: one for the poor, one to accommodate the strangers and 
the third for our personal needs. Since we got married, my wife lives with me 
like a sister . Each of us sleeps separately. At night we wear sackcloth, and 
during daytime, we put on our regular attires. No one knows anything about 
our lives.” Here, Mary looked down and supplicated to the elder monk to 
keep their life secret until they repose.  
 
MARY MAGDALENE, ST. 
The Lord Christ healed St. Mary Magdalene (from ‘Magdala’) by driving 
seven unclean spirits out of her. She was one of the women who served the 
Lord in Galilee (Luke 8:1 -2). She also was present when He was crucified 
and went to His tomb  along with two others, to find the grave empty. 
According to the Gospel of St. Mark, she was the first to see the Lord Christ 
after His resurrection (Mark 16:9), and St. John added that the Lord entrusted 
her to carry a message to His brethren (John 20:11-18).

MARY (The martyr) 
This saint was born in Atrib. Later on, she got married to a good man 
called Theodore and gave birth to a son, whom they called Sergius. When her 
son went to the governor Kyriacos and confessed h is Christianity, the 
governor tortured him, brought the statue of an idol, and ordered him to 
worship it. The young man, instead, kicked the statue and it fell down 
shattering into pieces. Before such a scene, the governor Kyriacos instantly 
believed in Christianity, saying, “A god, who cannot save himself, how could 
he save others? ” The minister Ohius then came forward and took over 
torturing Serguis with fire and other means. When Serguis’ mother and sister 
arrived at the torturing spot, they kept weeping for seeing him in that manner. 
However, that minister ended up having Serguis’ head cut off by the sword. 
His mother, Mary, his father, and his sister then came forward and 
confessed the name of the Lord Christ, and had their heads cut off by the 
sword too. They all received the crowns of martyrdom on the 13th of Amshir. 
 [Female Martyrs of Christianity, p. 91] 
 
MATHOY, FATHER 
Ordained as a Priest: 
It happened that the elder Mathoy (Mathos) once came out of Raythu to go 
to Magdelon with his brother. The bishop of the area took hold of him and 
ordained him as a priest. Afterward, while they were having dinner together, 
the bishop said to him, “Forgive me, father, I know that you did not want 
that, but I dared to do it to be blessed through you.” The elder Mathoy 
humbly answered, “To some extent, my mind did wish it, however, 
something was disturbing me, that I do not want to get separated from my 
brother because I am not used to do my prayers alone.” The bishop  told him, 
“If you think he is worthy, I may ordain him as a priest too.” Fr. Mathoy 
answered, “I do not know if he is worthy or not; all I know is that he is much 
better than me.”  
The Concept of Perfection: 
Fr. Jacob told the following story about Fr. Ma thoy, “I was once visiting 
Fr. Mathoy, and when I intended to leave, I told him, ‘I wish I could visit the 
“Cells.” He answered, ‘Please, Greet Fr. John , for me.’ When I conveyed the 
message to Fr. John, he said, ‘Fr. Mathoy is an Israelite indeed, in whom  
there is no deceit”  (John 1:47).’ A year later, when I conveyed the good

MARY, THE VIRGIN THEOTOKOS. 
This saintly virgin was born in the city of Nazareth, where her parents 
lived. Her father Joachim was carrying sorrowful heart because he was 
barren. Her mother Ĥenna was very grieved too, and she vo wed to God with 
a contrite heart, saying, “If you give me a fruit, I shall give her back to Your 
Holy Temple.” When the fullness of time arrived according to the Divine 
Plan, the angel of the Lord came down and announced the good news to the 
elder Joachim,  who, in turn, told his wife Ĥenna about what he saw and 
heard. They both rejoiced and gave thanks to God. Then, Ĥenna conceived 
from Joachim and gave birth to a saintly girl, and they called her Mary.  
When Mary reached three years of age, her mother brought her forth to the 
Temple. There, she spent 12 years, during which she was fed by the hands of 
angels. When her parents passed away, the temple priests decided to betroth 
her to a good man to keep her and take care of her because it was not proper 
to kee p her in the Temple after reaching that age. Therefore, the priests 
gathered 12 pious men of the tribe of Judah to choose from among them one 
that they would give Mary to. The priests brought these men’s canes inside 
the Temple, and it so happened that a dove came and stood on the cane which 
belonged to Joseph the Carpenter. By that sign, they knew that the Lord 
selected Joseph, who was a righteous man, to take care of the young Mary. 
She remained with him until the Archangel Gabriel came down to bring her 
the good news that the Son of God would be incarnated within her. 
After the ascension of the Lord Christ to heaven, the Virgin St. Mary was 
always praying in the holy sepulture, anticipating the happy day in which she 
would be loosened from the bonds of th e flesh. Then, she was told by the 
Holy Spirit that she would soon depart from this mortal world. When it was 
the designated time, the disciples and the virgins of Mount Olive came to her. 
While the Virgin St. Mary was lying on her bed, the Lord Christ Him self 
came to her with thousands of angels around Him, comforted her, and told 
her about the perpetual happiness she was going to enjoy. Rejoiced, she 
stretched her hand and blessed the disciples and the virgins, and delivered her 
pure soul in the hands of her Son and God, who took her up to the high 
dwelling places. As to her pure body, they shrouded it and carried it to the

she would fall into the hands of the governor. Eventually, her presence

MARY, THE SHUT-IN ASCETIC, ST. 
A Noble Woman becomes a Nun: 
This St. Mary was born to noble parents, among the elites of Alexandria. 
While she was growing up, so many young men of prominent families came 
to her parents proposing to have their daughter in marriage. However, she 
always declined that re quest. Once her parents died, she distributed her 
inheritance on the poor and the needy, kept only a small portion; then she set 
forth to a convent near Alexandria. There, she put on the monastic attire, 
strove in so much worship for 15 years, and then she  was clothed in the Holy 
“Eskeem,” and put on sackcloth on her body.  
The Shut-in Ascetic: 
After having the permission of her mother -superior, she shut-in herself in

records.question: Who was St. Demiana and how was she martyred?
records.answer:
St. Demiana was born to two pious Christian parents near the end of the 3rd century AD. Her father, Marcus, was a governor in the Nile delta region. She was baptized in El-Mayma monastery when she was one year old [1].

St. Demiana was a leader of forty virgins who lived a life of faith and asceticism. When persecuted, she boldly confessed her faith in the Lord of heaven and earth and declared her readiness to die for His name. The governor ordered her to be tortured severely: she was placed in a chamber with sharp blades that tore flesh, beaten with iron combs, and had gypsum soaked with vinegar rubbed into her wounds. Despite these tortures, she remained joyful and counted herself unworthy to partake in the Lord Jesus Christ's sufferings. She was thrown into prison, where the Archangel Michael healed her wounds twice. The governor, enraged by her survival and the conversion of many people who witnessed her healing, intensified her tortures, including breaking her skull and skinning her body. A white dove came down from heaven and healed her wounds again. Finally, the governor ordered her beheading along with the forty virgins with her. Before her martyrdom, she confessed the Lord Jesus Christ and declared that by His name she would forever live. She was martyred on the 13th of Toba. Her body remains in a church built by Queen Helena near the town of Bilqas in the Nile Delta, where a convent dedicated to her is also located. Several churches in Egypt bear her name [2].

Soon after, the governor resumed his violence and cruelty towards the 
saints. He ordered the hanging of ‘Cosman’ and ‘Damien’ on two crosses, then 
to stone them. However, the thrown stones, before touching their bodies, 
reversed their course and headed towards those who were throwing them. As 
for their brothers, they were chained, cast betw een the two crosses, and were 
being shot with arrows from a distance, but here too, the arrows were returned 
towards those who shot them. That miracle caused all guards to flee. Then, the 
governor ordered them unchained and cast all of them into a fiery fu rnace for 
three days and three nights. God saved them from the fire. Then, the governor 
put them on hot iron beds; but the Lord brought them up unharmed. 
When the governor got tired of torturing them, he sent them to the emperor 
to deal with them. When the mother ‘Theodata’ strengthened her children and 
rebuked the emperor on his cruelty and his worshipping of the idols, he ordered 
cutting her head by the sword, and she received the crown of martyrdom. Her 
body remained cast on the ground, and nobody dared to bury it. St. ‘Damien’ 
cried out to those present: “O you inhabitants of this city; is none of you have 
mercy to cover and bury the body of this old woman? ” ‘Boctor,’ the son of 
‘Romanos,’ came forward, took the body, shrouded it, and buried it.  
When the emperor got to know what ‘Boctor’ has done, he ordered exiling 
him to Egypt, where he eventually received the crown of martyrdom. The next 
day, he ordered cutting the heads of ‘Cosman,’ ‘Damien,’ and their brothers, 
all of whom received the crowns of Life in the Kingdom of Heavens. 
When the era of persecution came to an end, several churches were built in 
their names, where the Lord performed so many signs and wonders. 
These saints are celebrated by the Church of the West on the 7 th of 
September and the 4 th Thursday of the Great Lent and by the Coptic Church 
on the 22nd of Hator and the 22nd of Paona every year. 
 [Hegumen Bishoi Abdel Messih: SS. Cosman and Damien]

DEMIANA AND THE FOURTY VIRGINS, SS. 
(The martyrs) 
Her Upbringing: 
St. ‘Demiana’ was born to two pious Christian parents near the end of the 
3rd century AD. Her father ‘Marcus’ was a governor on ‘El-Burullus,’ 
‘Zaåfaran,’ and the ‘Saysaban valley’ (northeast of Gharbiah governorate) in 
the Nile delta. When St. ‘Demiana’ reached the first year of age, she was 
baptized in ‘El-Mayma’ monastery, south of the city of ‘Zaåfaran;’ and her

idols gods when there is no god except the Lord of heaven and earth? I am 
prepared to die for His name’s sake, along with all those who are with me.” 
Provoked to anger, the leader ordered four soldiers to place the saint into 
the ‘Hinbazeen’1 chamber and to start her torture. The other virgins bitterly 
cried out when they saw their matron being pressed and her body being 
slashed. Then barely alive, the saint was thrown into prison. There, the 
Archangel ‘Michael’ came down at midnight and healed all her wounds. 
In the morning, the soldiers came to check up on her, expecting to declare 
her death to their leader, but to their amazement, they saw her free of any 
wounds. Provoked to anger, the leader assumed that ‘Demiana’ was a sorcerer, 
and he declared that all effort would be made to disable her sorcery. 
On seeing the saint was restored to full health, the multitudes cried out: “We 
believe in the God of ‘Demiana.’” So, the soldiers’ chief ordered killing them 
all, and considering that the saint was responsible for leading so many ‘astray,’ 
he put in his heart to double her tortures. He ordered combing her body with 
sharp iron combs, then rubbed into her wounds gypsum soaked with vinegar, 
but she kept being exultant, counting herself unworthy to partake of the  
passions of the Lord Jesus Christ. 
Then, she was cast again in jail. On the next day, the leader himself went to 
check on her expecting to see a corpse, but he almost collapsed when he saw 
her entirely healed by the Archangel ‘Michael’ who revisited her. He furiously 
tortured her in so many different ways: breaking her skull and skinning her 
body. A white dove came down from heaven, hovered above her, and healed 
her from all her wounds. 
Whenever that leader tortured her, the Lord was glorified in her. Finally, the 
leader ordered cutting her head off, together with all the heads of the other 
virgins with her, and all of them received the crowns of martyrdom.  
Before the sword struck the saint’s neck, the saint cried out: “I confess the 
Lord Jesus Christ; on His name I die, and by it, I shall forever live.”  
She was martyred on the 13 th of Toba. Her body is still there in the church 
built by Queen ‘Helena,’ the mother of Emperor ‘Constantine the Great’ (306-
337 AD), located close to the town of ‘Bilqas’ in the north of the Nile Delta. 
That church was consecrated by pope ‘Alexander I’ (312-328 AD) on the 12th 
of Bashons. Annexed to that church is the convent of St. ‘Demiana.’  
Several churches were built all over Egypt in the name of this great martyr. 
 [El-Mahaba Bookstore: The Biography of St. Demiana]

Because of those healing wonders, the prison guard ‘Lucius’ proclaimed his 
faith in the Lord Christ. In the meantime, the puzzled governor ‘Degnianus’ 
set the bishop free. 
His Baptism: 
After ‘Lucius’ was baptized on the hands of St. ‘Theodorus,’ he tried to draw 
the governor and the judge to the Christian Faith. He managed to succeed in 
convincing the governor but failed with the judge. Then, both ‘Lucius’ and 
‘Degnianus’ left the country and set forth to the island of ‘Cyprus.’ There, 
‘Lucius’ proclaimed his faith before the governor of that island, who ordered 
his head to be cut off, and he received the crown of martyrdom. While 
‘Degnianus’ spent the rest of his life on the island leading a holy Christian life. 
[Martyrdom in Christianity; p. 131] 
 
DELPHINUS, THE BISHOP , ST. 
This saint was the bishop of the city of ‘Bordeaux’ (in southwestern France), 
and he reposed in the year 403 AD. This saint’s fame was generated because 
of the letters he exchanged with St. ‘Ambrose’ ( 374-397 AD), and also, 
because of his influence on St. ‘Paulinus,’ whom he converted to Christianity 
and was baptized by him. 
[Butler: December 24] 
 
DEMETRIAS, THE NOBLE VIRGIN 
St. ‘Demetrias,’ this lady saint belonged to a noble family in Rome, and she 
dedicated her life to God i n virginity. Her grandmother, on her mother’s side, 
was so pious to be commended by St. ‘Jerome.’ She had three sons, all of whom 
were consuls. ‘Demetrias’ was longing for a life of virginity; however, she was 
afraid of the opposition of her parents, but they approved with joy and pleasure. 
The dedication of her life to God became the cause of happiness for all the 
churches. 
St. ‘Jerome’ (347-420 AD) encouraged her to study while she was pursuing 
a life of worship. He sought from her to be careful in choosi ng her friends or 
those among whom she lives. He preferred for her the life of fellowship rather 
than a life of seclusion; to practice the evangelic life among them; the way he 
previously guided ‘Eustochium,’ ‘Paula’s daughter;’ thirty years earlier. 
In the year 414 AD, St. ‘Jerome’ sent ‘Demetrias’ his letter # 130, in which 
he presented to her the basic principles to which she should be committed in 
her new life. His letter came to clarify the ascetic life in conjunction with the

In the meantime, the King of Persia ‘Shapur II’ (309-379 AD) was on good 
terms with the Roman Empire and used to pay taxes to the Roman emperors. 
However, he changed his position and came with his army to fight the Romans 
in the days of Emperor Julian the Apostate (360-363 AD). Emperor ‘Julian’ 
offered sacrifices to his idol ‘Apollon’ in the city of ‘Casius,’ six miles from 
Antioch, then he marched with his army, accompanied by the diviners and the 
sorcerers, to encounter the Persians. 
Julian persecutes Domicius: 
When emperor ‘Julian’ was passing through an isolated site, he noticed a 
large crowd of men, women, and children; and he was told that they were sick 
Christians who came to get healing by the prayers of Fr. ‘Domicius’, the man 
of God, living in a cave over that area. 
The emperor was provoked to anger, and he sent a soldier to threaten the 
saint, saying: “If you dwell in this cave to please God, why do you seek the 
pleasure of dealing with people,  while you should have hidden from them? ” 
The saint answered him: “I have delivered my soul and my body into the hands 
of the God of heaven and earth; the Lord Jesus Christ, and I live as a hermit in 
this cave. However, those crowds who come to me with their strong faith, I 
cannot send them away.” 
On hearing his answer, the emperor gave his orders to shut the entrance of 
the cave with rocks while the saint was trapped inside. So, the saint eventually 
delivered his soul and received the crown of martyrdom in the year 362 AD. 
 [Baring-Gould’s Lives of the Saints: August 7] 
 [The Synaxarion: 27 Baramhat]  
 
DOMINICA, THE VIRGIN, ST. 
(The martyr) 
This saint was living at the time of emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD), and 
she was accused of breaking the idols down. The emperor ordered to cast her 
to the wild hungry beasts . However, the beasts did not harm her. So, they cut 
her head off around the year 303, and she received the crown of martyrdom. 
 [Butler: July 6]

morning.’ When all the brethren stood to pray in the morning, they asked 
the saint, ‘Tell this brother to stand up to pray, O father.’ The saint did, and 
the evil spirit came out of the man, and he was instantly healed.” 
Of His Words: 
A brother once asked the saint , “Father, what should  I do?” The saint 
answered him: “Keep quiet, and consider yourself as nobody.” 
“Have great care, you monk, to refrain from committing any sin, lest you 
insult God who dwells within you, and drive Him out of your soul!” 
   [W. Budge: The Paradise of the Holy Fathers, Vol.1, 2] 
 
BIBIANA (VIVIANA), THE VIRGIN, ST. 
(The martyr) 
A church was built in Rome under the name of St. ‘Bibiana’ (Viviana), in 
the 5th century AD. 
It was said that she was martyred in the days of Emperor ‘Julian the 
Apostate’ (360-363 AD). She was the daughter of ‘Flavian’ (Flavianus), who 
was the governor of Rome. He was known for his zeal about the Christian faith 
with his wife ‘Dafrosa,’ and on that account , he was fired from his position, 
was branded on his forehead w ith hot iron, and was exiled to a place called 
‘Aquapendente’ (the water of the bull), where he died in exile. 
The Western Church celebrates his memorial on December 22. As to his 
wife, she was put under house arrest, together with her two daughters ‘Bibiana’ 
and ‘Demetria.’ Finally, the head of St. ‘Dafrosa’ was cut off. Her memorial is 
celebrated by the Western Church on the 4th of January. 
The two girls ‘Bibiana’ and ‘Demetria’ stayed in their house, but they were 
in great need after all their possessions were taken away from them . They 
practiced prayers and fasting follo wing a harsh ascetic way for five months. 
However, the new governor ‘Abronianus’ kept threatening them every day of 
torture if they would not deny their Christ.  
Finally, he brought them for trial before the court of justice . During that 
trial, St. ‘Demetria’ fainted and collapsed, and then delivered her pure soul to 
the Lord. Then, the governor brought her sister ‘Bibiana’ to an evil corrupted 
woman by the name of ‘Rufina,’ to lure her to sin and to seduce her to deny 
her faith with empty devious promises . St. ‘Bibiana’ totally rejected all the 
advances of that evil ‘Rufina,’ and in spite of being beaten viciously by 
‘Rufina;’ sometimes using whips and other times by iron nails which tore off 
her flesh, the virgin ‘Bibiana’ endured the torture with great pe rseverance.

337 
 
persist in disobeying the orders of the emperor. At the same time, he promised 
to add to their wealth if they obeyed. The saints, remembering the teachings of 
their parents and their good role model, they were not  terrified by the threats, 
nor seduced by the promises. They bravely answered him that they despise this 
world with everything in it , and were ready to die a thousand times than to 
deny the Lord Christ. On intensifying the mental and physical torture of those 
two virgin saints, Dimetria delivered her soul before her sister Vivian, and she 
received the crown of martyrdom on the 21st of June 363 AD. 
St. Vivian, who came to be lonely, by the grace of God, she kept unshaken 
before all those horrible events . Besides, she kept rebuking the cruel , unjust 
man on his evil behavior and sought from him to remember his end, and how 
it would be as dark as his heart. 
Vivian delivered into the hands of an evil Woman: 
To seduce Vivian to submit to his evil ways, Apronianus delivered her into 
the hands of a wicked woman named Rufina, who was extr aordinarily artful 
and was determined to bring her to another way of thinking. That agent of hell 
employed all the allurements she could invent , which were afterward 
succeeded by blow s. However, Vivian, making prayer her shield, remained 
invincible. On seeing that all his attempts ended up in failure, Apronianus felt 
that he ha d been severely belittled before that girl . So, he was provoked to 
anger and ordered that she would be bared naked, tied to a pillar and scourged 
with a whip loaded with lead plummets . Under that whipping, she delivered 
her pure soul into the hands of her true Groom , the Lord Christ, and she 
received the crown of martyrdom on the 2nd of December 363 AD.  
They left her body in a location without burial for several days to be 
devoured by the stray dogs and wild beasts. However, the Lord kept her body-
safe, and no beast could touch it . Eventually, a sa intly priest called John, 
managed to take her body and bury it beside her sister Dimetria and her mother 
Dafrosa. After a while, a pious Roman lady called Olympia built a little church 
in their names in the palace of their father Flavian. She also moved their bodies, 
buried them underneath the altar, together with the pillar to which St. Vivian 
was tied . In the Western tradition, the martyr Vivian is considered as the 
intercessor for people deserting the habit of getting drunk and also for the 
people who have epilepsy and severe headaches. 
  [The Martyrs: Vivian, Christine, Julia, Juliette and Auginie; p. 10] 
  [Saint Bibiana: From Wikipedia the Free Encyclopedia] 
       [Butler: 2 December]

DIONESA, THE DEACONESS 
On the 13 th of Baramouda, the Coptic Church celebrates the feast of 
‘Dionesa,’ the deaconess, who was appointed by the apostles. 
[The Synaxarion: 13 Baramouda] 
 
DIONYSIA, ST. 
(The martyr) 
In the days of persecution stirred up by Emperor ‘Decius’ (249-251 AD), in 
the year 250 AD, in the city of ‘Troas’ in Asia Minor; three Christians were 
presented to the governor, their oldest was a man called ‘Nicomachus,’ who at 
the beginning confessed his faith, and refused to sacrifice to the god, but when 
they started torturing him, and the pain was too much for him, he cried out, “It 
is a mistake. I never was a Christian; I shall sacrifice to the gods.” They brought 
him down from the tool of torture; but the moment he put the flesh of the 
sacrifice on his lips, he fell dead, as a denier. 
A 16 years old girl called ‘Dionysia,’ observing this scene, cried out. “Poor 
miserable man, for the sake of a few moments of pain, you earned for yourself 
indescribable eternal pains.” Then, she was brought before the governor who 
inquired from her if she was a Christian. She answered him: “Yes, I am; that is 
why I am sad for that miserable man who could not endure a few momen ts 
more to gain eternal comfort. ” The governor sought from her to do likewise, 
or else she would be tortured and burnt alive. 
The next day, ‘Andrew’ and ‘Paul,’ the companions of ‘Nicomachus,’ were 
brought before the judge, who decided to deliver them to the mob to stone them 
to death. Their feet were tied together and were dragged outside the city to be 
stoned there. Meanwhile, ‘Dionysia’ was led to receive her final verdict, when 
she met the crowd that was dragging ‘Andrew’ and ‘Paul’ to their death. On 
seeing them passing by, she managed to get away from her guard and cast 
herself on the two of them, crying: “Let me die with you upon the earth, that I 
may live with you forever in heaven,” but the governor denied her request and 
ordered cutting her head off by the sword. 
[Martyrdom in Christianity, p. 164] 
 [A. J. Mason: The Historic Martyrs of the Primitive Church, 1905, pp. 137 -9]

Her Persecution: 
On failing to convince St. Juliana with showing his compassion,  the 
governor started to use violence and torture with her. Six of his shrewdest men 
whipped her until they were utterly exhausted. During all that time, she did not 
cease to repeat: “O my Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of God, Come to my help.” 
They beat the saint harshly for a long time, but after each beating , she 
received healing and new strength from God . Her punishment took place 
before a large number of people. Of these, 500 men and 150 women came to 
confess Christ after witnessing the courageous holy virgin miraculously healed 
from her severe wounds . They were all beheaded and were baptized in their 
blood. Then, the governor commanded to cast her into prison. 
There, she confronted and fought against Satan face to face, and prevaile d 
over him. Satan took the form of an angel of light, and tried to convince her to 
forsake her faith, and submit to the will of her father in the flesh and to the 
governor who tortured her. (Because of that, her old icons portrayed her tying 
a winged Satan with chains). Then, they continued her torture . They tore her 
flesh with iron claws and immersed her in boiling water . However, these 
tortures did not harm her. Finally, St. Juliana was sentenced to death and earned 
the crown of martyrdom by having her head cut off around the year 304 AD. 
 [Butler’s The Lives of the Saints: February 16] 
 
JULIANA (The martyr) 
St. Juliana (Yuliana) was present at the time when governor Marcianus was 
torturing St. Barbara in the days of Emperor Maximianus in the 3 rd century 
AD. Juliana was so impressed, and believed in Christianity when she saw how 
the Lord Christ comforted and strengthened St. Barbara. Getting to know that 
Juliana converted to Christianity, governor Marcianus ordered cutting off her 
head on the 8th of the Coptic month of Kiahk. A church was built on the location 
where she was buried and was dedicated on the 26 th of Kiahk. Her biography 
could be found together with that of St. Barbara under the letter ‘B’:  St. 
Barbara. 
 
JULIANUS OF ANCYRA (The martyr) 
This St. Julianus was a priest in Ancyra at Galatia. He was martyred during 
the persecution by Emperor Licinius I (E: 308-324 AD) at the beginning of the 
4th century AD. His memorial is celebrated by the Western Church on the 13th 
of September every year.

torment with great courage. The pagans kept screaming at them, seeking 
from them to save themselves by sacrificing to the gods, but the saints 
answered them, saying, “We are Christians, and we prefer to die thousand 
times than to do what you ask us to do.” 
After a while, the governor realized that he was defeated before them. So 
he gave his orders to his men to cut the Saints heads off. The saints, with 
courage and joy, approached the swordsmen while praying to God to have 
mercy on their souls, on those of all other men, and to save their fellow 
citizens from the darkness of idol worship. After cutting their heads, the other 
believers came and buried their bodies, which were moved to Rome. 
Later, the Fathers who assembled in the Council of Crete in the year 458 
AD, wrote to Emperor Leo I (457 -474 AD), saying. “The blessing and 
intercession of those Ten Martyrs have protected their country so far against 
the heresies.” The village where the saints were tortured was named “The Ten 
Martyrs.” Also, a large broken stone was discovered in the location where 
those ten saints knelt down to receive the crowns of martyrdom. They found 
that this stone had ten depressions resulting from the strikes of the shar p 
blade during the saint’s execution. 
 [Butler: December 23] 
 
MARTYRS OF DANDARA 
On the 16 th of Bashons, the Coptic Church celebrates the memory of the 
martyrdom of 400 martyrs in the town of Dandara (on the west bank of the 
Nile, about 5 kilometers south of the city of Qena). They were executed after 
suffering many tortures because they were Christians. This happened near the 
end of the reign of Emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD). 
 [The Synaxarion: 16 Bashons] 
 
MARTYRS OF EDESSA 
In the days of Caesar Trajan ( 98-117 AD), there was a violent persecution 
against Christians in Edessa (El -Roĥa) in the Syrian section of Upper 
Mesopotamia. The bishop Barsimaeus (Barsamya) was arrested, violently 
tortured, and martyred in the year 114 AD. However, according to another  
version, he was only arrested but not killed; then, he was released after the 
persecution and later on reposed in peace.  
Among those who were martyred was Sarbelius and his sister Barbea, who 
were baptized by the bishop Barsimaeus; and they were martyred  during the 
persecution. Sarbelius in particular was viciously tortured because he was

check on her, to carry the news of her death to the Caeser, he was amazed to 
see her standing in prayer, with no trace of any wounds but signs of inner peace 
and joy on her face. Here, the soldier cried out, confessing the God of this saint. 
His confession was repeated by so many of the prisoners who heard his account 
about what he saw. And, all of them were executed by the governor. 
A Friendship with a Hungry Lion: 
To turn that saintly virgin into an example to anyone else who would dare 
to confess the Lord Christ and refuse to worship the idols, the governor ordered 
casting her into the arena in the presence of people and State officials, to be 
devoured by a hungry lion which was left for three  days without food . 
Everybody among the spectators anticipated seeing a vicious , bloody 
encounter at the critical moments. However, to their surprise, they saw the saint 
standing in prayer with full grace and true peace. Then, the l ion, shaking the 
arena with its loud roars, and instead of devouring the saint, they saw it quietly 
approaching the saint and then bowing its head in submission to lick the saint’s 
feet with its tongue like a domesticated cat . Many of the spectators cried out 
confessing the God of St. Tatiana; and the governor ordered them executed by 
the sword. 
Accusing Her of Sorcery: 
To justify their failure and weakness before God’s work in the life of 
martyrs, the governor and the judges accused the saint with using sorcery. The 
governor ordered to cast the saint into a fiery furnace. Because of its intense 
heat, the two soldiers who pushed the saint into the fire were inflicted with 
severe burns. However, God saved St. Tatiana the way He did with the Three 
Young Men in the Old. Feeling the intense shame, the governor finally ordered 
cutting the saint’s head with the sword; and she received the crown of 
martyrdom. The West celebrates her martyrdom on the 12th of January. 
 [Bishopric of Girga: Paradise of the Female Saints, p. 4]

She was married to a man from the family known as Fruia. She got attached to 
the family of the two saints Paula and her daughter Eustochium . These two

son married Blaesilla, the daughter of Paula, and her daughter Furiam married

records.question: search saint: Verena
records.answer: Saint Verena was a virgin from the town of Garagous in the district of Qus in the governorate of Qena. She was a nurse and a relative of St. Victor (Boctor), one of St. Maurice’s associates, and she joined the military in the Theban Legion, which was sent to Switzerland. Verena was in Milan when she learned that St. Maurice, St. Victor, and the other members of the Theban Legion were martyred by order of Emperor Maximian (286-305). She traveled to Agaunum to bless the bodies of those martyrs and to seek the relics of St. Victor. Afterwards, she lived as a hermit in Solothurn, Switzerland, dwelling in a cave and going to nearby villages to offer mercy and kindness to the poor. She fasted and prayed continuously, and several miracles were attributed to her intercession. Verena was a spiritual counselor for young girls and cared for their physical health due to her nursing expertise. It is said she spent the rest of her life in a cave near present-day Zurich in Germany. Her piety influenced the local people so much that after her repose, they built a church over her grave, engraving her portrait carrying a pitch and a comb. This church was destroyed in the 9th century during Germanic invasions, and later a Benedictine monastery was established on the site. St. Verena remains honored and appreciated throughout Switzerland [1][2].

VENERIUS, BISHOP OF MILAN, ST. 
St. Venerius was one of the deacons of St. Ambrose, bishop of Milan (374-
397). St. Venerius became the bishop of that city in the year 400 AD, after the 
repose of St. Simplician (397 -400), who succeeded St. Ambrose on the 
diocese. Little is known about the biography of this saint, beside s that he was 
very much supportive of St. John Chrysostom during his tribulations, and that, 
when the bishops of Africa assembled in Carthage in the year 401 AD, they 
sent him a message of support and encouragement. He reposed in the year 408. 
 
VERENA, ST. 
St. Verena was a virgin of the town of Garagous in the district of Qus in the 
governorate of Qena. And, as a nurse and a relative of St. Victor (Boctor), one 
of St. Maurice’s associates, she also joined the military in the Theban Legion, 
which was sent to Switzerland. 
Verena was still in Milan when the word was received that St. Maurice, St. 
Victor, and the other members of the Theban Legion, who had proceeded north, 
were all martyred by order of Emperor Maximian (286 -305). Verena traveled 
to Agaunum, where they were killed to have the blessing of the bodies of those 
martyrs and to look for the relics of St. Victor, her relative.  
Afterwards, she led the life of a hermit in a place called Solothurn (in 
Switzerland), she dwelt in a cave from which she used to go to the villages 
around to offer acts of mer cy and kindness to the villagers and the poor. As a 
hermit, Verena fasted and prayed continuously . Several miracles were 
attributed to her intercession. Verena was a spiritual counselor for young girls, 
and due to her expertise as a nurse, she used to look after their physical health. 
It was said that she had spent the rest of her life in a cave near present -day 
Zurich in Germany. Her piety had such a great influence on the people in the 
area, that when she reposed in peace, the people in that region built a church 
over her grave, on which they engraved her portrait carrying a pitch and a 
comb. That church was destroyed along with the whole village when the 
German tribes invaded the region in the 9th century. Later on, a monastery for 
the Benedicts was established on that site. St. Verena is still the object of honor 
and appreciation all over Switzerland. 
 [The Story of the Coptic Church; Book 1, p. 140]

he would finish his prayers, the fever and headache would forsake him. By that 
way, this monk was able to overcome the adversary thoughts. 
5. Controlling the Mind: The saint was asked: “How could man reject the 
talk of laymen in temporal issues; and how could he keep his mind with God , 
as it is written?” She answered: “This is like sitting at a banquet with many 
kinds of foods. If you eat with greed and covetousness, you would be guilty. If 
you eat without greed or covetousness, then you are not guilty. It is the same 
if you listen to the talk of laymen, but keep your heart with you, and have no 
pleasure in what being said. you would be unharmed.” 
6. The Features of a Teacher: It is befitting of a teacher to be a stranger to 
the desire of authority, pride and vainglory; lest he would pr obably fall by 
flirtation and lose his vision by gifts. But it is befitting of him to be 
longsuffering, meek and humble, as much as he can, and does not seek 
appearances, but cares for all and loves everyone. 
7. Enduring Tribulations: Let us try to enter t hrough the narrow door. For 
unless a tree endures the tempests of winter, it would not be able to produce 
fruit. For us, this age is like a stormy winter; it is only by enduring the 
tribulations and the temptations, we would inherit the Kingdom of Heaven. 
8. Sanctification of the Body: In a debate concerning the body between a 
Christian and a Mani -follower, the Christian said: “By letting the body walk 
according to the Divine law, you will find it on the side of its Creator.”  
 
THEODORA, EMPRESS 
This saint Theodora (~500-548 AD) was the wife of Emperor Justinian I 
(527-565). She was one of the most prominent women of the old , known for 
her beauty, iron will, riches and firmness, along with her broad knowledge. 
In the year 523, Justinian married her, and in the year 527, she was crowned 
as an empress. She had an active role in the theological debates and was very 
vibrant in other activities . Contrary to her husband, she loved St. Severus of 
Antioch and supported the non-Chalcedonian Egyptian Church. 
She had a significant role in the ethical reforms, cared for pious works, and, 
together with her husband, they cared for building churches and hospitals. 
She reposed in the year 548 AD. Her portrait in the mosaic was found in the 
Basilica of San Vitale in Ravenna. 
   [Cross: Dictionary of the Christian Church, p. 1358] 
 
 
THEODORA, THE BURRIER OF MARTYRS

345 
 
unceasingly. Give God thanks for everything. 
 A brother asked him: “What makes the life of a monk?” He answered: “A 
mouth that says the truth; a holy body and a pure heart.” 
  “Unless Moses has gathered first the sheep he was tending in one group 
before he went to see the amazing scene of the Burning Bush; his attention 
would have been distracted by the worrying about the flock scattered in the 
wilderness. So it is the same with the monk, if he longs for the purity of 
heart, by which he can see God; he  is committed first to forsake all his 
earthly possessions, his feelings, and desires, and to live in perpetual retreat, 
in which he gathers his mind, and keep it from scattering and diversion; and 
to have one and unique goal to look at God. By this, he would be qualified 
for the purity of heart and enjoy God and his proclamations.” 
 Walk along the sabsolute path; count the miles, and do not be careless. 
        [Palladius: The Paradise, ch. 12]  
 
BERTANUBA, THE VIRGIN, ST. 
(The martyr) 
The Coptic Church celebrates her feast on the 21st of Toba (Synaxarion of 
Rene Bassett). The story of that young virgin shows how much so many people 
care for the life of purity and virginity.  
It was said that the twelve years old St. ‘Bertanuba’ was very beautiful, lived 
in Rome, loved the life of virginity, and joined a convent in the mountains of 
Rome. On hearing about her beauty, the Emperor ‘Constantine the Great’ (306-
337 AD) sent his men to bring her over for him to see her . The emperor' s 
messengers were amazed by her beauty that they took her along without the 
permission of the mother-superior. The virgins tearfully bid her farewell, and 
she asked them to pray for her sake that God may save her from this trial. 
Before Emperor Constantine: 
She stood before Emperor ‘Constantine’ with her heart up in heaven, and 
her mind was occupied with a concealed prayer to God. She prostrated herself 
to the ground before the emperor , and when she stood up and saw a golden 
cross on his throne, she was exalted and encouraged. Seeing how beautiful she 
was, the emperor became very excited and sought from her to enter into his 
private section to talk freely . There, the girl prostrated herself again to the 
ground before him , and then she stood up to say: “Live forever, my l ord 
emperor.” He responded to her by saying: “I intend, ‘Bertanuba’ to lift you up 
and to honor you. I forsook all the women in the world and sought you to be 
my wife, not to become a maidservant, but an absolutely free lady, who possess

passages.text:
204 
 
support those who follow the true Faith."  
The Emperor could not answer him with a single word; for when one of 
those present reviled the saint and threatened to kill him, he instantly fell dead, 
which terrified the emperor and kept him from stretching his hand to harm the 
saint; despite the provocation of the Arians to send him into exile. 
A little while later, ‘Valens’ died in a fire; and the Church was relieved from 
his oppression. The saint returned to his seclusion, to resume his prayers for 
the sake of the whole world until he reposed around the year 345 AD. He is 
celebrated by the Greek Church on the 29th of January and by the Latin Church 
on the 7th of April. 
 
APHRATES, FATHER 
He was one of the Fathers of the wilderness who has given a living example 
for the monk who rejected any gift from anyone. He trusted only in God, 
saying: “If God allows me to live, then God knows how to fulfill my needs; 
and in case if He doesn’t, why should I live?” When he came to be an invalid 
cripple, on the bed of sickness, he refused to receive any gift from anyone, 
saying: “If I take anything from anyone, I have nothing to reward him with!” 
He believed that the true believer should not care for being reviled or 
oppressed, for his eyes should always b e focused on God and seeing no one 
else. He said: “It is befitting for those coming to God, to look at Him only and 
to take refuge humbly in Him and nobody else. In this way, they would 
disregard any revile or oppression targeting them, even if it occurred  ten 
thousand times!” 
 
APHRONIA 
(The martyr) 
Her Monastic Life: 
St. Aphronia lived in Mesopotamia, ‘Almissah.' When her heart kindled 
with the love of God and was longing to dedicate all her energies to worship, 
she joined a convent. In that convent, her a unt ‘Auriana’ was the mother -
superior, so she became one of her disciples. She was very keen on the study 
of the Holy Bible and on practicing the monastic life with enflamed zeal. 
Her Martyrdom: 
When Diocletian stirred up persecution against the Christians, the 50 virgins 
in the convent, out of fear forsook the convent and went into hiding. Only 
‘Oriana,' the mother -superior, Aphronia, and another nun remained there.

But, it happened that an evil man, noticing how the older woman frequently 
came out to the mountain; he followed her from afar, came to know the cave 
into which she used to enter, and he hid until she came out and went her way. 
That evil man, assuming that she has hidden some valuable articles there, so 
he entered into the cave looking for that treasure. However, he found the three 
brides of Christ praying. The evil man bound them with ropes and brought 
them forth to the governor of Thessalonica. The governor on questioning them, 
he was told that they were Christian worshippers of the Crucified. He was 
provoked to anger, and he tortured them and cast them in the fire, where they 
delivered their souls and received the crowns of martyrdom. 
 [The Synaxarion: 8 Baramouda]  
 
SHIRIN, ST. 
A Spiritual Guide for the Monks: 
St. Shirin (a Persian word meaning beautiful) lived in the 6 th century. She 
was not a nun, but a regular woman who lived in the world, yet in a way more 
ascetic than many of those who worshipped God in the wilderness. She was a 
spiritual guide to so many, including monks and nuns 
According to her biographer, the monk  Martyrius Saådona, she lived in a 
town called Halmon, of a simple family in a region called Beth Nohad in 
northern Iraq. She used to get up very early in the morning to pray before 
starting any work; and in the evening she prayed together with the whole 
family to give thanks to God for allowing their day to pass in peace. She went 
regularly to the church with her family. In this manner, the saint was raised in 
such a beautiful spiritual atmosphere; she despised the pleasures of the mortal 
world and kept on reading the Holy Bible and reciting its verses all day long, 
even while working. 
Her Virginity: 
Her prudence and purity becoming well -known, many right persons came 
to propose to marry her. But, she refused all and told her parents that she 
desired to be a bride of the Lord Christ and only preoccupied with Him. Due 
to her parent's great love for her and not to offend her, they decided to leave 
her alone to handle her personal life with freedom. 
Ascetic in her food, the saint, calmed down her hunger by eating dried bread 
and some boiled vegetables in the evening and drinking some water, yet her 
countenance, by the grace of the Holy Spirit, much shone with light. 
She used to pray all the time by reciting Psalms and some short prayers and

and come to me." 
Her Repose: 
Abba Daniel perceived that it was time for her departure, and he while wept 
bitterly. Then, he set forth to go to her with his  disciple, telling him: “Woe to 
the inner wilderness, for a pillar, will fall in it. Come, my son, bring the tools 
and let us hasten to reach the elderly saint before we are deprived of his 
prayers, for he is departing to the Lord." When they reached her, they found 
her severely ill with fever. After she received the Divine Sacrament, she made 
the sign of the Cross on herself, and her face shone, then she delivered her soul, 
and instantly, a sweet fragrance spread around the place. 
The two men wept, dug a g rave in front of the cave, and Abba Daniel 
instructed his disciple to shroud her over her clothing. Then, they buried her 
and prayed. On their way back, the disciple informed his mentor that he 
accidentally saw her dried up breasts. Then, Abba Daniel told him her story, 
and how the Roman elites diligently sought her and how no one knew anything 
about her up till that moment. 
She reposed in the year 576 AD. The Coptic Church celebrates her on the 
26th of Toba; whereas the Greek and the Latin Churches do on t he 10 th of 
March. 
 
ANASTASIA, SAINTS by that Name: 
(The martyr) 
The traditional books of Martyrs and the biographies of the Monks 
introduced to us many ladies who carried the name ‘Anastasia’ in the early 
centuries. The adoration of the Christians for the Lord Jesus Christ and being 
perpetually preoccupied with the power of His resurrection working within 
them made this name genuinely dear to them. Since the word ‘Anastasia’ 
means “Resurrection." In the following few articles, we shall mention some of 
the most famous of those who carried that name. 
 
ANASTASIA, ST.  
(The martyr) 
This Saint was martyred in the days of Emperor ‘Decius’ (249-251 AD) 
around the year 250 AD, and celebrated by the Coptic Church on the 1 st of 
Baba... 
She was the daughter of Christia n parents in Rome; they raised her in fear 
of God. Her heart was full of the Love of God, longing for the angelic life of 
virginity since her childhood. She joined a convent in Rome to practice the

maidservants free . In the Ethiopian Synaxarion ,1 it was recor ded that this 
saint reposed on the 21st of the Coptic month of Baba. 
 
MARIAN AND JAMES, SS. 
Those two saints were martyred in Lambesa in Numedia , during the 
persecution agains t the Christians stirred up by Emperor Valerian  (253-260 
AD). Marian (Marianus) was a reader in the church, and James was a deacon, 
and both of them were arrested in Kyrta (nowadays Constantine  in Algeria). 
They were taken to be heavily tortured . After inten se torture, in a night -
vision, Marian reported that he saw St. Cyprian, who was martyred in the 
previous year, calling him to martyrdom , while James saw in a night -vision 
too that he was very close to the victory. 
After they were tried before the governor, they were sent for execution to 
Lambesa, eighty miles away. That place was like a river' s valley, with its 
banks gradually ascending on the two sides as though they were seats in a 
huge theater. In that valley, the line of martyrs was so long, and the swords of 
the executioners kept striking the necks of the believers, one after the other . 
Before it was Marian' s turn, he talked by the spirit of prophecy about the 
horrible end waiting for the murderers of the believers . They finally cut his 
head off, and his mother took his body in her bosom, kissed it , and buried it 
besides that of his companion James. Their martyrdom took place in the year 
259 AD. 
 [Butler: April 30] 
 
MARINA, THE HERMIT, ST. 
This is a biography of a girl who challenged the rules of nature . She 
clothed herself in the attire of men, to be able to practice the tough ascetic life 
with joy. Also, she was wrongly accused of committing a great sin, which 
brought on her troubles until the moments of her departure . Without 
defending herself, she man aged to move heaven to defend her after she 
reposed; and to come to be the cause of the repentance of so many. 
Her Upbringing: 
Most probably, St. Marina was born in the land of Bithynia on the 
northwestern part of Asia Minor during the 8 th century AD . She was the 
daughter of a very rich man, and she was called Mary. When her mother died 
while she was a little infant , her pious father Augatius  raised her well and

her peace, and healed her of her wounds. The next day, when a soldier came to 
check on her, to carry the news of her death to the Caeser, he was amazed to 
see her standing in prayer, with no trace of any wounds but signs of inner peace 
and joy on her face. Here, the soldier cried out, confessing the God of this saint. 
His confession was repeated by so many of the prisoners who heard his account 
about what he saw. And, all of them were executed by the governor. 
A Friendship with a Hungry Lion: 
To turn that saintly virgin into an example to anyone else who would dare 
to confess the Lord Christ and refuse to worship the idols, the governor ordered 
casting her into the arena in the presence of people and State officials, to be 
devoured by a hungry lion which was left for three  days without food . 
Everybody among the spectators anticipated seeing a vicious , bloody 
encounter at the critical moments. However, to their surprise, they saw the saint 
standing in prayer with full grace and true peace. Then, the l ion, shaking the 
arena with its loud roars, and instead of devouring the saint, they saw it quietly 
approaching the saint and then bowing its head in submission to lick the saint’s 
feet with its tongue like a domesticated cat . Many of the spectators cried out 
confessing the God of St. Tatiana; and the governor ordered them executed by 
the sword. 
Accusing Her of Sorcery: 
To justify their failure and weakness before God’s work in the life of 
martyrs, the governor and the judges accused the saint with using sorcery. The 
governor ordered to cast the saint into a fiery furnace. Because of its intense 
heat, the two soldiers who pushed the saint into the fire were inflicted with 
severe burns. However, God saved St. Tatiana the way He did with the Three 
Young Men in the Old. Feeling the intense shame, the governor finally ordered 
cutting the saint’s head with the sword; and she received the crown of 
martyrdom. The West celebrates her martyrdom on the 12th of January. 
 [Bishopric of Girga: Paradise of the Female Saints, p. 4] 
 
TATIANA 
St. Tatiana was a noblewoman of Rome at the end of the 4th century AD.. 
She was married to a man from the family known as Fruia. She got attached to 
the family of the two saints Paula and her daughter Eustochium . These two

records.question: Tell me about St. Rebecca and her five children.
records.answer:
St. Rebecca was a widow and mother of five children named Agathon, Peter, John, Amon, and Amouna. They lived in Kemola in the district of Qus in Upper Egypt. Rebecca was devoted to raising her children in the Lord’s ways, and their hearts were filled with exalted love for God. They experienced a night vision in which Archangel Michael appeared to them, proclaiming that they would receive the crowns of martyrdom near Alexandria, and that their bodies would be moved to Naqraha in El-Behairah governorate [1].

When Emperor Diocletian ordered the destruction of churches and persecution of Christians, St. Rebecca encouraged her children to hold fast to their faith, reminding them of Jesus’ words about tribulation and not fearing death. They prayed for mercy on the Church and strength to remain faithful. An angel appeared to them, comforting and assuring them of the crowns of martyrdom. They distributed their possessions to the needy and appeared before Dionysius, governor of Qus, who demanded they burn incense to idols. They refused, confessing their faith in the Lord of heaven and earth, and endured severe torture with courage and joy. Many witnesses were inspired to proclaim their faith and were martyred as well. Rebecca and her children were imprisoned with many bishops and priests [2].

Because Agathon was popular, they were sent to Armenius, governor of Alexandria, who tortured them by pulling out their teeth and imprisoned them. Archangel Michael appeared again, healing and encouraging them. The next morning, they were seen without wounds and proclaimed their faith, leading the governor to order their execution. When placed on iron beds over fire, God sent rain to extinguish the flames, and more people converted and were martyred. The governor then ordered their bodies stabbed and wounds soaked with vinegar, but the Archangel healed them again and told them their crowns were near. They were finally hanged upside down, put into boiling oil which spilled over the soldiers killing them, then beheaded. Their bodies were cast into the sea [3].

A rich Christian man was instructed in a night vision to retrieve and keep their bodies until persecution ended. Their relics were moved to St. Mina Church in Debi, then to Sonbat in the province of Zefta, where a church was built in their name. Their martyrdom is commemorated on the 7th of Tout [3].

sang the hymns with humi lity, some members of the Society of El -MaĥAbba 
sought from him to join their Society, which he was happy to do. 
His Care to Search for the Lost: 
Ragheb Sawires founded the Society of the Children of the Apostles, which 
had a vital role, beside s ministering as deacons, of searching for the lost, to 
bring them back to the Church and to reconcile the rival families . On his tall 
crutches and frail body, he persisted in chasing the lost, even if he had to climb 
so many steps up to people living on great stories in the middle of the night. 
Together with the members of his Society, they divided themselves into 
teams to go to visit the poor quarters , which did not have any churches or 
enough pastoral care. 
That faithful energetic minister did not live long. He reposed in peace while 
he was just 44 years of age; on the 14th of February in the year 1945. 
  [The Faithful Synaxarion: 7 Toba] 
  [The Story of the Coptic Church; Book 6, p. 186] 
 
REBECCA AND HER FIVE CHILDREN (The martyrs) 
Archangel Michael Appearing to Them: 
The story of St. Rebecca (Refqa) and her children shows how much a 
Christian family would be willing to do to enjoy the Heavenly Crowns. 
Nothing did occupy the heart of this widow beside s the thought of enjoying 
the Divine bosoms along w ith her five children , no matter how much that 
would cost them . Hence, this family did not lose their happiness amid their 
sufferings. On the contrary, their labors turned into a source of collective joy 
for the whole family and a living testimony before t he people to learn from 
their experience. In the meantime, as the hearts of the members of that family 
were raised to heaven, God sent His angel several times to support them and 
bring happiness to their suffering hearts. For the holy life is a source of joy to 
the striving believers, as well as to the Heavenly Hosts. 
This woman was widowed, as a mother of five children: Agathon, Peter, 
John, Amon, and Amouna. They were living in Kemola of the district of Qus 
in Upper Egypt. Their mother cared very much in raising her children in the 
Lord’s ways, and their feelings were kindled with the exalted love of God. 
In a night vision, Archangel Michael proclaimed to them that they would be 
receiving the crowns of martyrdom near Alexandria; and their bodies would be 
moved to Naqraha in the governorate of El-Behairah (near Damanhur).

Preparing for Martyrdom: 
Having enjoyed seeing the Archangel Michael, the mother and her children 
were filled with joy and anticipated the time they would receive the crowns of 
martyrdom, for which they were prepared their whole life. 
When Emperor Diocletian (284-305 AD) ordered destroying the churches, 
burning the Holy Bible and torturing the Christians until they deny faith; St. 
Rebecca urged her children to hold fast to their faith; and reminded them of 
the saying of the Lord: “In the world, you will have tribulation” (John 16:33); 
and “Do not fear death.” And, she told them that the most precious gift a person 
could give is his own life, if he gives it without hesitation or remorse, but with 
courage and joy. They kept supplicating to God to have mercy on His Church 
and to hold His people fast in the faith. 
While praying, when an angel of the Lord appeared to them, proclaimed 
that they w ould receive the crowns of martyrdom in the name of Christ, 
comforted and gave them the good news: “God be with you, and will give you 
strength until you consummate your strife; so do not fear death, but testify  to 
the Lord.” Then, they were filled with a fantastic, joyful peace. 
When it was time, they distributed their possessions on the needy , then set 
forth to appear before Dionysius, the governor of Qus, who asked them to burn 
incense before the idols . They all cried out, saying: “We are Christians, and 
only worship the Lord of heaven and earth, in whose hands are all men .” 
Attempting to no avail to seduce them by many gifts, the governor threatened 
to kill them if they persisted on confessing the name of Chri st, to which they 
proclaimed their longing to die, to encounter their beloved Christ face to face. 
So, the governor tortured them severely, starting with their mother, who 
endured with perseverance and kept encouraging her children . They, too, did 
endure torture with courage and joy, that many of those present proclaimed 
their faith in the Lord Christ and were martyred. Then, the governor ordered to 
put the saint and her children in prison, which was already packed with a 
multitude of people, together with bishops and priests. 
Before Armenius, the Governor of Alexandria: 
As the older son , Agathon was popular in the town and so beloved by his 
fellow citizens, and because of him and his mother and brothers, many were 
martyred; some counseled the governor to se nd them to Armenius, the 
governor of Alexandria, where no one there knew them. Because Armenius, at 
that time , was at Shubra, they were sent to him there; he tortured them by 
taking their teeth off, then cast them in prison, where the Archangel Michael 
appeared to them again, healed and encouraged them. In the morning, when 
the guards and the people were amazed to see them with no sign of wounds on
