Book 7: Eschatology and the After Life 
475 
Fourth: Our Lord Jesus has not cheated us. According to the martyr St. Cyprian, 
“For he who [spiritually] wars for God, dearest brethren, ought to acknowledge himself as 
one who, placed in the heavenly camp, already hopes for divine things, so that we may 
have no trembling at the storms and whirlwinds of the world, and no disturbance,  since the 
Lord had foretold that these would come. With the exhortation of His fore -seeing word, 
instructing, and teaching, and preparing, and strengthening the people of His Church for all 
endurance of things to come, He predicted and said that wars, and  famines, and 
earthquakes, and pestilences would arise in each place; and lest an unexpected and new 
dread of mischiefs should shake us, He previously warned us that adversity would increase 
more and more in the last times. ‘Behold, the very things occur w hich were spoken; and 
since those occur which were foretold before, whatever things were promised will also 
follow; as the Lord Himself promises, saying, But when you see all these things come to 
pass, know that the kingdom of God is at hand ’ (Luke 21:31) . The kingdom of God, 
beloved brethren, is beginning to be at hand.”1175 
Fifth: So that the body may be formed again without sin. St. Gregory of Nyssa is of 
the opinion that the body must die if it is to be formed anew and restored to its original state 
without any of the sin that accompanied it during its life on earth. He likens the human 
body to an earthen vessel into the very material of which poison has infiltrated. It must be 
shattered and treated to remove all traces of the poison, and then re -molded if it is to be 
restored to its original state when it was safe to use and devoid of poison. This is all 
through God’s immense love for us, here in this world, through the blood of the Lord 
Christ. We are sanctified in our entirety ; although the war of the fl esh with sin remains, 
which is why we remain in need of being completely remade through the merits of the 
precious blood.1176 
Sixth: The Lord has changed the very concept of death. Once our Christ willingly 
accepted death for the salvation of the world, it became no longer a punishment that  
terrifies the believer, but rather a sign of the love that he desires. A believer accepts death 
for the sake of God, for the salvation of his fel low believers, for his own growth (going 
through it every day as a communion with the crucified Christ), and as a living promise of 
the eternal life. According to St. John Cassian: “Not in fear and terror, but with a spirit of 
hope, awaiting eternity, with out dejection but with the eyes of the spirit does the believer 
look upon the exercise of dying daily in order to live. Thus, he sees with every breath that 
his spirit is being constantly renewed, as though his body is being gradually transformed 
from flesh into spirit … longing to behold the last day … he moves into a state of perfect 
knowledge when he sees God face to face.”1177 
 
1175 St. Cyprian of Carthage, Treatise 7: On the Mortality 2 (ANF 5:469) amended.  
1176 See St. Gregory of Nyssa, The Great Catechism 8–9, 16–17, 25–26, 28, 32 (NPNF II/5).  
1177 St. Cassian, Institutes 5.41.

Book 3: The Church: The Kingdom of God 
519 
Himself engraves them on incorruptible tablets. He  writes them with His finger as He did 
with the law of the Hebrews.”1312 
The Church was first and foremost concerned with the intentions of the person seeking 
to be baptized, as mentioned in the  Apostolic Tradition of St. Hippolytus : “Those who 
come forward for the first time to hear the word … let them be examined as to the reason 
why they have come forward to the faith. And those who bring them shall bear witness for 
them whether they are able to hear … If he be the slave of a believer and his master permit  
him, let him hear. If his master does not bear witness to him, let him be rejected … If a man 
have a wife or a woman a husband, let them be taught the man to be contented with his wife 
and the woman to be contented with her husband.”1313  
In his homily to the catechumens, St. Cyril of Jerusalem says, “The honesty of purpose 
makes you called: for if your body be here but not your mind, it profits you nothing. Even 
Simon the sorcerer once came to the Laver: he was baptized, but was not enlightened; and 
though he dipped his body in water, he enlightened not his heart with the Spirit: his body 
went down and came up, but his soul was not buried with Christ, nor raised with Him.”1314 
684. How long was the teaching phase of the catechumens? 
Registering the names of catechumens who wish to be baptized at the beginning of Lent 
and examining them did not mean that that was when their relationship with the Church 
began. Prior to this, they often stayed under the patronage of the Church for three years, 1315 
during which the y proceeded from one order to the next, until the Church was assured of 
their good intentions, sincerity in seeking salvation, dedication to the faith, and godliness. 
Only then could they move on to the last stage of the catechumenate which is that of the 
candidate for baptism. The pace of this transition varied from one person to another, 
according to each person’s zeal, and their level of prior knowledge of the faith. In the  
Apostolic Tradition of St. Hippolytus, “If someone is truly zealous, he should be accepted. 
Time does not matter as much as the conduct.”1316  
The three stages of the catechumenate were the following:

passages.text:
Book 7: Eschatology and the After Life 
531 
indebted to the sanctified soul; for she has submitted to the Holy Spirit of God and 
sanctified her will, having invested her joy in obedience to the commandment of her 
beloved God. She has invited the Savior to establish His kingdom within her and walked in 
truth by the spirit of adoption by the Father. Likewise, the soul  realizes its debt to the body 
which exercised its senses in the spirit of holiness, and strove to study the Holy Bible, fast, 
pray, and keep vigil in the spirit of praise. There is no room for reproach between them; 
when the believer stands on the Day of the Lord, he is g rateful for His work in his soul, 
body, and all his faculties.  
St. Augustine says, “Because so perfect shall then be the harmony between flesh and 
spirit, the spirit keeping alive the subjugated flesh without the need of any nourishment, 
that no part of o ur nature shall be in discord with another; but as we shall be free from 
enemies without, so we shall not have ourselves for enemies within.”1286 
1418. How shall the body and soul of an evil person be reunited, given that he has not 
given himself a chance to return to God? 
It seems to me that they would blame one another. The soul would feel that the body 
with its desires has pushed the person as a whole to love the world, to refuse to return to 
God, and to be apathetic about encountering Him and accepting the divine grace that would 
have been capable of establishing the kingdom of God within that person . And the body 
would feel that the soul is responsible for the straying of the will, and for all the  hatred 
towards others and denial of the grace of God the person has practiced. In this manner, the 
wicked person spends his life in conflict, even in hell. The body cannot stand the soul, and 
the soul cannot stand the body. They are in unceasing bitternes s and under the 
condemnation of the doomed — yet they never perish. 
In short, in Christ Jesus , love and eternal life prevail, even between the soul and the 
body; but in hell, bitter conflict prevails, even between the soul and the body. 
1419. How are the dead raised? And what body will they have? (1 Cor. 15:35). 
The first of these questions is posed by unbelievers to those who believe in the 
resurrection of the dead , that is : “by what power, or by what means is it possible to 
accomplish resurrection?” In their vi ew, this is impossible. The second question is : 
Assuming that resurrection is possible, will they rise with exactly the same appearance and 
body members? The first question is the question of an  atheist who cannot fathom the 
power of God to raise the dead;  and the second question arises from  the curiosity of a 
skeptic. 
 
1286 St. Augustine of Hippo, The Enchiridion 91 (NPNF I/3:266).

The apostles desired for men to be very

In this order,
and by this succession from the apostles, the ecclesiastical tradition and the
preaching of the truth have come down to us. This is the most abundant proof of
the one vitalizing faith, which has been preserved in the Church from the
apostles until now and handed down in truth.
Since

others. Truth is easy to obtain from the Church because the apostles, like a

robbers. On this account we are bound to avoid them,

tradition of truth.

In the 2

Many early Church Fathers opposed the Gnostics

One was St.

of “tradition” may be summarized in the following points:
1. The tradition originating from the

65. How has the Holy Bible been preserved till today? 
The Holy Bible is the book of the Church, which we receive through the tradition of the 
Church. By tradition, our sacred books were canonized, confirming that they were divinely 
inspired. Origen the scholar says, “in all these questions we approve of nothing but what the 
Church approves of, namely only four canonical Gospels.” 203 St. Cyril of Jerusalem  says 
”Learn also diligently, and from the Church, what are the books of the Old Te stament, and 
what those of the New.” 204 So also St. Augustine: “For my part, I should not believe the 
gospel except as moved by the authority of the Catholic Church.”205 St. Basil the Great says, 
”For were we to attempt to reject such customs as have no writ ten authority, on the ground 
that the importance they possess is small, we should unintentionally injure the Gospel in its 
very vitals.”206 
It is important to note that while Church tradition testifies to the Holy Bible, and the Holy 
Bible is itself a part of the Church’s tradition, none of this diminishes the unique value of the 
Bible. Tradition defends the Bible’s nature as the word of God, the eternal divine revelation, 
which addresses not only the present age but also the ages to come.  
Although tradition testifies to the Holy Bible, it cannot be its judge. On the contrary, a 
tradition is only accepted if it is founded on the Bible; it cannot be accepted if it disagrees 
with the Holy Bible.207 
Moreover, the Holy Bible is for every believer, that he may experience it and personally 
taste its beauty, appreciating its value and inspiration. However, no one can by himself 
determine the divine inspiration of the Holy Bible and the presence of the Holy Spirit within 
the Bible — only the Holy Spirit who lives in t he Church can do that.  It is not through any 
individual effort of a human deciding alone, but through adherence to the judgment of the 
Church.208 
Finally, the close relationship between the Holy Bible and the tradition of the Church in 
no way extinguishes o ne’s personal feelings towards the Holy Bible. On the contrary, the 
tradition of the Church reinforces the personal approach, and requires of us that we live the 
Bible in no way isolated from the Church.

Origen discussed two problems faced by the
early Church concerning the Old Testament:
1 - The Jews expected the Messiah would
fulfill the prophecies of the Old Testament literally, such as He must be their
King who reigns over the whole world. Therefore, they refused Jesus as the true
Messiah.
[175]
2 - The Gnostics rejected the Old
Testament, for they were scandalized by some passages that refer to God as
being angry or that He regretted or changed His mind... They were scandalized
because they interpreted them literally and not spiritually
[176]
Origen saw that these two groups
misinterpreted the Scripture since they held the literal sense exclusively.
Therefore, he set his theory that there are three various meanings in
Scriptures -- the literal, the moral and the spiritual.
According to Origen, the words of the
Scriptures should be imprinted in people's souls in one of three ways
[177]
1-
Rustic people or the uneducated
should be edified by the letter itself, conceived as the obvious meaning in a
straightforward historical sense.
2-
People with a higher level of
education
should find edification for their souls by the moral meaning.
3-
The sublime
should be edified by
the mystical sense of a relationship with Christ, or the spiritual Law, as it
contains the portent of blessings to come.
Man is composed of body, soul and spirit,
and the structure of Scripture has been planned by God for man's salvation in
the same way.
Origen found in the Ark of Noah a
materialization to his theory since it was built in three levels. The bottom
served as the foundation, which refers to the literal or the historical
explanation of Scripture, the higher is the spiritual or the mystical level,
while the middle represents the moral level.
[178]
According to Origen, the understanding of
Scripture is "the art of arts" and "the science."
[179]
The words of the
Scripture are its body, or visible element, that hides its spirit or invisible
element. The spirit is the treasure hidden in a field, hidden behind every
word,
[180]
every letter and even behind every iota used in the written word of God.
[181]
Thus, "everything
in the Scripture is mystery."
[182]
This spiritual understanding of the Scripture is grace given to the perfect
believers by Christ. For only those who have the Spirit of Jesus can understand
their spiritual meaning,
[183]
i.e., to enter this chamber of eternal
marriage between Christ and the soul.
We obtain this grace through prayer, as we
must weep and beg the Lord to open our inner eyes, like the blind man sitting
by the roadside at Jericho. (Mat. 20:30) Origen says that we must pray, for we
are often beside the wells of running water -- God's Scripture -- and we yet
fail to recognize them by ourselves.
The Law is a shadow of the Gospel, and the
latter in turn is a shadow of the kingdom to come. In one of his commentaries
on the Canticle of Canticles, Origen explains this relation between the Law and
the Gospel by saying:

wall. The wall was the Old Testament, and He stayed behind it until He revealed

Himself at the windows. The windows were the Law and Prophets, the predictions
that had been made about Him. He began to be visible through them. He began to
show Himself to the Church, who was sitting indoors, i.e., she was engrossed in
the letter of the Law. He asked her to come out and join

days and seven nights, and on Sunday, when his spiritual father came out to go 
to the church, he found St. Joannes the Short lying down outside the cell and 
the angels placing seven crowns of light on his head. That spiritual father 
hastened to welcome him inside the cell with love and joy.  
His Love for the Salvation of Others: 
The repentance of the lady saint Paisa will remain a living testimony of the 
profound caring of St. John the Short - who was preoccupied with the 
contemplation in the Divinities - for the salvation of others. 
His Compassion on Others: 
While the saint was traveling in the Sc etis along with some brethren, it 
happened that their guide lost his way in the darkness of the night. Abba John 
told the brethren: “I shall pretend that I am so tired that I cannot walk any more; 
and that I need to rest until the morning. For, if we alert  our guide, he might 
become embarrassed and feel uncomfortable.” So they did, and in the morning 
they quickly found their way. 
Healing the Sick: 
St. Joannes the Short was granted from God the grace of healing the sick. 
Among the accounts which were written about him, the following stories: 
Once, the saint encountered in a field a farmer inflicted with leprosy. The 
man sought his prayer to be healed. He prayed on some water, gave it to him 
to drink, anointed him in the name of the Holy Trinity, and the man was healed 
and glorified God. Another time, a woman came to him, she was possessed by 
an unclean spirit that tormented her quite often. The saint had compassion for 
her and prayed on her behalf. The unclean spirit came out of her, and she was 
healed. 
He once encountered an older woman who asked him bread for herself and 
her blind son. The saint gave her all the bread that he had; prayed for the sake 
of her blind son; made the sign of the Cross on his eyes, and he instantly was 
able to see. 
In the doxology of  Abba Joannes the Short, it came: “You came to be a 
haven for salvation; you raised the dead, drove the demons out, and healed the 
sick. You became worthy, O father Abba Joannes, to sit together with the 
Apostles to judge your generation.”

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 3, p. 14
passages.text:
14 
 
was in the middle of the wilderness of  the Scetis, and the third was not far 
from the inhabited area. 
His Transparency: 
The disciple of St. Macarius narrated about him, saying: “I was told by my 
spiritual father: ‘No Saturday or Sunday pass without me seeing the altar 
angel near me, while I am offering the Sacrifice .’” Besides, it was repeatedly 
said that whenever the saint used to enter the Holy Sanctuary to consecrate  
the Holy Sacraments, he would see how it was full of angels and saints, and 
he used to become overwhelmed by profound fear and awe. 
His Fight against the Vainglory: 
Troubled by tho ughts of pride and love of vain glory, as the evil planted 
thoughts that kept provoking him to go to Rome, the land of the emperors, to 
heal their sick, he sat at the entrance of his cell and dared the demons, saying: 
“If you have enough power, move me by force from here.”  
Also, when the demons pressed him harder, he cried out in  anger: “I have 
already told you that I do not have legs anymore; if you have the power, carry 
me to Rome. Otherwise, I shall stay here until sunset.” 
Again, when he was disturbed by these same evil thoughts in the middle 
of the night , he got out of his ce ll carrying a big basket he filled with about 
eight gallons of sand, and he kept wandering in the desert while carrying that 
big load . Then, when the br ethren saw him, they asked: “O f ather, why 
should you do such a thing? Why would you tire yourself?”  The saint 
answered them, “I tire who tires me; because if I give him comfort, he would 
bring vain thoughts to my mind, and provoke me to go outside.” He then kept 
walking in the desert all night and came back to his cell, dead tired. 
The Bunch of Grapes: 
It happened once that someone brought to St. Macarius  a splendid bunch 
of grapes, which he has not tasted for so long. Yet he overcame his desire and 
gave the bunch to a sick brother , who, in turn, gave it to another, counting 
him more in need for it . The bunch of grape kept on being carried from one 
cell to another until finally it was brought back intact to St. Macarius, who 
rejoiced in the lovely relationships between the monks . (Some believe that  
this incident happened to St. Macarius the Great). 
His Miracles: 
The saint managed to heal a countless number of sick people and those 
who were possessed by evil spirits. He was granted that power that by merely 
making the sign of the Holy Cross on those people, they would get healed.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 157
passages.text:
157 
 
A Wonder-Maker: 
As many miracles and signs were performe d on his hands, in the name of 
God, multitudes came to him from Persia, Ethiopia, France, Spain, England, 
and Italy, to seek counsel and healing from St. Simeon. Kings and bishops 
came from Europe to ask him about specific issues, which he answered 
according to the guidance of the Holy Spirit, and many people put his portrait 
in their houses for a blessing. As testified by his disciple Theodoret, who saw 
it by his eyes, being burdened by having his hands kissed and his robe touched 
for blessing by many, he made for himself a six cubits (1 cubit=1.73 feet) high 
pillar; increased it by six cubits, then by 8 cubits more, to reach 30 cubits high 
[= 52 feet]; with a top circle of 6 spans (1 span=9 inches) wide [= 4.5 feet], 
surrounded by a low fence to keep him from falling off. 
St. Simeon drew many believers to repent. He had a fantastic influence on 
pagans who proclaimed their faith in the Savior of the world. And, he was the 
cause of comfort to so many who came to listen to his sermons. 
The Repentance of a Thief: 
Antiochus Agonatus, the head of a gang of thieves, had such a very strong 
body, that he was feared even by soldiers. When he went too far with his 
crimes, a large regiment of soldiers was sent to chase him. Finding him in a 
night club, once he raised hi s sword, they were so terrified that he could flee 
away. By the grace of God, he went to St. Simeon to present repentance with 
tears. When the soldiers came to arrest him and asked the saint how he would 
protect such a criminal, He answered them that the t hief came to him seeking 
the mercy of God and offering repentance. 
When the soldiers withdrew, the saint sought from the thief not to resume 
his crimes. The thief cried out, exploring the mercies of our Lord Jesus Christ, 
raised his hands toward heaven, and said: “O my Lord Jesus Christ, the Son of 
God, receive my spirit.” Crying for two hours, the saint and all who were 
present, were so impressed that they all cried when they saw the thief lean his 
head on the pillar, and then deliver his soul. 
A Man of Prayer: 
Once his disciple was watching the saint praying and started to count the 
number of times of his kneeling (metanoias). The disciple scored 1,240 
metanias that the saint did, then he stopped counting. 
It was said that when an elite came to visit the saint, the man implored him, 
saying: “In the name of Him who incarnated for our sake, I beg from you to 
tell me; Are you a human or of another creation, which appears as human?” 
Here, the saint sought from his disciple to bring a ladder and to let the man

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 159
passages.text:
159 
 
the people; two of them approached him and said that they were sent by the 
elders, to tell him that, by so doing, he deviates from the way of virtue and 
follow a way different from that of the saints. And, they said to him that the 
elders were ordering him to come down from his pillar.  
On seeing how Simeon instantly sent his disciple to bring a ladder and 
intended with humility to come down his pillar, the two messengers said to 
him: “We are now sure of your obedience. May God is with you, and may His 
Spirit guide you in this unique way. Keep it on, do not come down, for so have 
those who sent us commanded us to do.” 
Compassion on those who intended to Kill Him: 
It happened that three armed thieves, with the assumption that the saint had 
collected plenty of money given to him by his countless visitors, they came to 
kill him and take all that he had. Once they aimed their arrows against him, the 
arrows returned towards them, so they fell motionless and speechless. Next 
day, when they revealed their identity and confessed their evil intentions, the 
saint prayed for their sake, healed them, after warning them not to do it against 
anyone else lest more harm would dwell upon them. 
A Man of Authority: 
The saint felt that he was granted the authority over evil by the Lord Christ 
his Savior, so it happened that the devil brought to him a horrible serpent that 
curled around his legs. Without confusion and in full peace, he did not interrupt 
his prayer, and the serpent split into two and died. 
Another time, when the devil came to him in the form of a colossal dragon 
to devour him, he raised his eyes toward heaven and addressed the dragon, 
saying: “May God strike you.” And it instantly disappeared.  
Sanctifying the Day of the Lord: 
As the saint cared for sanctifying the day of the Lord; a group of people 
approached him to complain that their spring of water has dried up and their 
fields were getting wasted. He answered them: “I feel that there is something 
you intend to hide from me. Now! Be honest, and confess that. Because one of 
you watered his plantation on a Sunday, the spring dried up.” He rebuked them, 
warned them not to do it again, sough t from them to put a wooden cross on 
three stones, throw them into the water, scatter dirt in the form of a Cross on 
the spring of water and keep on praying all night. When they did so, they saw 
the amazing work of God as water resumed flowing from the spr ing, and it 
covered their fields.

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 79
passages.text:
79 
 
the Great. He practiced the life of solitude in the Western Desert, in the  
province of ‘El-Ashmonein.' He lived in a cave in which he shot himself in to 
contemplate. Despite his strict asceticism, he did not cease to practice the 
handwork to give to the poor. He also cared to counsel the brethren, and God 
granted him the gift of  performing miracles. In other words, his solitude was 
founded on an open heart full of love for God and men. His disciple ‘Ephraim’ 
gave us a concise account of his life. 
His Life as a Monk: 
The saint was born to Christian parents; they raised him on the fear of the 
Lord. He grew loving the life of seclusion and contemplation, together with 
his love for the needy. 
While still a young man, he spent a lot of time among the monks and was 
trained on the ascetic life and the handwork to be able to give alms to the poor. 
When he became a monk, his love for solitude grew stronger that he lived in a 
very dark cave, where God granted him a fountain of water to drink from. He 
trained himself on fasting, by eating once a day in summer and once every two 
days in winter . He practiced the perpetual prayers and was making 300 
metanoias by day and 300 by night until his skin stuck to his bones and came 
to be as a burnt stick. 
A Spiritual Center: 
Despite his great love for the life of solitude, he did not shut off his heart 
nor his cave in the face of his brethren. But his dwelling place turned into a 
center of spiritual radiation. The elder monks residing on the mountain used to 
come to seek his counsel, and he used to inflame their hearts with longing for 
the Christian perfection in the Lord. 
His Prophesying About the Death of the King: 
His disciple once saw him sad, and on asking him about the reason, the saint 
told him that on that day, the soul of emperor Theodosius the Great was sought, 
and the bonds of the State order w ere about to come apart. The disciple made 
a note of the prophecy date, and after some time, when he descended to the 
world, he came to know that the emperor has died on that exact day. 
Examples of His Miracles: 
1- A priest once came to him inflicted with a s kin disease that exposed the 
bone of his forehead. And, despite the persistence of his disciple in seeking 
from the saint to come out and pray for the sick priest, he did not pay 
attention to him. Finally, he explained to his disciples that, because the 
priest has defiled the house of God by adultery and taking the church money 
to spend on his evil desires, he had no liberty to seek healing from God. 
Later on, he had compassion on him and asked his disciples to tell the priest

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 351
passages.text:
351 
 
In this matter, he said: “Woe of him who is concerned with what on the 
outside more than that on the inside (meaning: Woe to that who sees the outer 
sins of his brother and does not see his inner sins).” 
God's Wonders through Him: 
St. ‘Bessarion's’ disciple told those stories:  
 “The saint was traveling along a road, and he came to the river 
‘Chrysoroan,’ and there were no means available for crossing it . The saint 
then stretched out his hands and prayed and crossed over to the other side . 
When I saw that, I was amazed and gave the saint a metonia and asked him: 
‘Father, while you walked on the river, how far up did your feet felt the 
water under you?’ To which he answered: ‘As far as my ankles, but all the 
rest of it was solid underneath my feet!’” 
 “On our way to visit one of the great wise men, it was going to be sunset 
before we would have reached our destination . The saint then prayed: ‘O 
Lord, keep the sun in its place until I reach Your servant,’ and God granted 
him his request.” 
 “I came once to talk to him in his cell, to see him standing while extending 
his hands towards heaven and praying. I waited for four days and four nights 
until he called me, saying: ‘Come  my son.’ Then, we went out and kept 
walking, and in our way, I got thirsty and said  to him: ‘Father , I am very 
thirsty.’ He separated for a little distance and prayed, then came back to me 
carrying water in his robe, out of air!  I drank it, and we kept going on our 
way to ‘Lycopolis’ (Assiut) to Abba ‘John.’ After greeting one another, the 
saint prayed, sat, and told him about a night vision he saw. He said: ‘From 
the Lord, a decree came that all the temples of the idols will disappear ,’ 
which happened at the time.” 
 “A man in Egypt had a paralyzed little boy . H e carried him to Abba 
‘Bessarion,’ then he left him crying at the door of his cell and went a little 
distance away. On hearing the voice of the little boy, the saint came out to 
see him, and he said to him: ‘Who are you?  And how did you get here?’  
The little boy answered: ‘My father brought me here and went his way, and 
here I am crying .’ The saint told him: ‘Get up and run after him .’ The 
paralyzed boy was instantly healed and ran after his father , who was so 
happy for that miracle, and they went their way.” 
 “Another time, a man with an evil spirit was brought to the church, where 
prayers were raised for him. However, the demon did not come out of him. 
The priests then said, ‘No one can drive him out except Abba ‘Bessarion ;’ 
but if we asked him to do it, he will not even come to the church. We shall, 
therefore, do the following without telling him in advance . We shall place

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 465
passages.text:
465 
 
"Did I clothe you well enough, my son?" All those present heard a voice from 
the dead man, saying: "You have clothed me well, my father, according to your 
promise." Everybody was amazed and glorified God. Then, the saint set forth 
to the wilderness, fleeing from the vainglory.  
However, the saint used to return periodically to his monks and disciples, 
to take care of those who would need help or were sick among them. 
Raising a Dead Man: 
It happened once that St. ‘Petarpemotis’ went out to visit a sick brother, who 
was suffering severely during his hours of death. His conscience grievously 
tormented him because of his many sins that he did not repent for yet. The saint 
asked him: "How can you go to the Lord while carrying the proof o f your 
slothfulness in your works?" The brother begged him to pray on his behalf to 
God to grant him a little more time to mend his life and ways. The saint told 
him: "How dare you ask for more time to repent when your life has already 
come to an end..?" However, because of the miserable feeling of that brother, 
the saint prayed to God, and then he told the brother: "God has granted you 
three years more." Then, he held his hands, helped him up, took him along to 
the wilderness to live with him for the duration of those three years.” 
Prayer on the Sand: 
Once a farmer came to Abba ‘Copres’ carrying a bucket full of sand. The 
saint was questioned by his visitors: “Why did that farmer come to you with 
the sand bucket? ” The saint said: “Sometime ago, the village next to the 
monastery was inflicted with worms which devoured their crops. The monks 
here prayed on some sand and asked the farmers to mix it with their fertilizers 
when they were planting, and the prayers on that sand stopped the worms, so 
it became a custom until now that the farmers would bring us sand to pray over 
it for them to use it with their fertilizers.” 
Accepting the Robber of Faith: 
According to Abba ‘Copres;’ a believer had a garden in which he dedicated 
its fruits to the monks. A pagan robber sneaked into it and stole some of its 
fruits. He tried to cook them on fire for three hours; the water did not boil, and 
the fruits remained uncooked. So, the robber brought the fruits to the saint, 
begging for forgiveness, and asked him to make him a Chri stian. The saint 
received him and instructed him about the Christian principles. 
[St. ‘Jerome’s “On Illustrious Men”: Translated to Arabic by Deacon Michael Max 
Iskander]

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 3, p. 403
passages.text:
403 
 
The man woke up to find himself before that pious woman who was 
wondering and asking him: “What are yo u doing here, man? What do you 
want? Who are you?” He answered her: “I do not know, but I beg you to tell 
me where I can find a Church.” She took him to the church, where he threw 
himself at the feet of the Fathers and asked them to convert him to a Christian 
and show him how to repent. He narrated the story of his life to the Fathers, 
and they were amazed to hear it. They started to guide him gradually and 
taught him the psalms. 
Three days later, he left the place and set forth to the wilderness to live fo r 
five weeks eating no bread, until someone begged him to do so. For three 
years he kept weeping with tears, praying to God to forgive him. Then, he 
finally returned to the church to learn more about the Christian faith. Even 
though he was illiterate, he m emorized the Holy Bible by heart. Amazed at 
what he has reached of knowledge, asceticism, and piety; the priests in the 
church baptized him and sought from him to stay with them, but after a week, 
he set forth to the inner wilderness to remain there for se ven years. During 
that time, every Sunday, he would find a loaf of bread by his pillow to eat and 
to continue fasting from one Sunday to the next. 
His Fatherhood and Miracles: 
At the end of the seven years, St. Petarpemtis returned from the wilderness 
bearing exalted spiritual virtues within himself, along with fantastic 
simplicity and strong asceticism. So, many others followed his example; 
mostly, they were young men. 
According to St. Palladius (386 -430 AD), this blessed man, whenever a 
Christian man woul d die, used to stay beside his body the whole night 
praying, then he would shroud him and bury him. On seeing him doing that, 
his disciple, longing to have the same portion, asked his mentor: “When I die, 
Father, will you do the same to me?” The father ans wered him: “I shall do 
this until you say Enough”. After a long time the disciple passed away, and 
his mentor stayed beside him the whole night; then he shrouded him by 
himself in the Divine fear and reverence; and while everyone was watching, 
he said: “Ha ve I, my son, shrouded you well, or is there anything more you 
want me to do?” To the astonishment of all, they heard a voice coming out of 
the corpse (body), saying: “You shrouded me well, Father, and fulfilled your 
promise to me.” Those present got filled with fear and glorified God. 
The saint kept on going back and forth between the wilderness and the 
dwelling place of his disciple, and it happened once he was going back to his 
disciples, and some of them were inflicted by fever; the sun was about to set , 
and he felt that he should not walk in the darkness; following what the Holy 
Bible said: “ Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtakes you”

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 2, p. 260
passages.text:
260 
 
Gaining the Blessing of the Holy Land: 
St. Hilarion kept on moving around in the Sinai desert . Then, he set out to 
get the blessing of the Holy Land , which was sanctified by the Lord  Jesus 
Christ, who lived there for a while . He also visited the monasteries there, 
enjoyed the encounter with the saintly monks and nuns, in whom he smelled 
the sweet fragrance of Christ.  
Father of the Monks: 
However, during his wandering in that area, a high number of young men 
gathered around him seeking to be his disciples, since they were impressed by 
his imposing role model of holiness, love, and humility, which were planted in 
him by Abba Anthony.  
So, as the monks gathering aroun d him increased in number, St. Hilarion  
built monasteries for them. He became a father for all of them and kept visiting 
every monastery once every year to guide the monks and to hold them fast unto 
Faith. He became so burdened with labor, especially with the increasing crowd 
of those who came to seek his prayers and blessing. 
The Saint Gets Attacked: 
It happened one day that Hilarion was attacked by armed robbers while he 
was kneeling to pray. When he disregarded them and kept on praying , they 
asked him: “Don’t you fear us?”  He answered, saying: “He who possesses 
nothing would fear no one !” When they added: “We could kill you!”  He 
answered them: “I don’t fear death  because I am always ready for it!” 
Perceiving the true faith through him, they were filled with fear and repented 
before him. St. Hilarion was attacked several times by the devi l: once in the 
form of women to corrupt the purity of his mind . Other times in the way of 
wild beasts to terrify him . Yet, he kept being armed with prayers and making 
the sign of the Cross on himself and managed to live in the peace of God. 
God's Miracles performed on His Hands: 
In the city of Eleutheropolis (Beit Guvrin near Hebron), a barren 
noblewoman came to seek his prayers to ask God to give her a child. Running 
away from her, she kept chasing him while bitterly weeping . He finally had 
compassion on her, blessed her, and told her: “My daughter, be sure that God 
responded to your request.” The following year, she came to him carrying her 
child, and the news spread all over the area. 
When the miraculous works of God kept happening again and again through 
this saint, multitudes of people came to seek his prayers . Many pagans 
proclaimed their faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, and a lot of believers asked him

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 2, p. 191
passages.text:
191 
 
She reached perfection in every virtue that even any one of them would have 
been enough in place of all the others. 
We have seen in the biography of this saint, how the nature of women could 
surpass that of men, in her strife for salvation . It tells us that the discernment 
between men and women is only physical and has nothing to do with the 
spirit!” Here, we will  try to mention some of the well -known general facts 
about this saint, even though her Christian principles made her hide what she 
enjoyed. 
Her Carriage Flipped Over: 
“Once, the horses of her carriage ran so crazily that her carriage flipped 
over, and she was inflicted with serious wounds and bruises on the outside with 
internal bleeding on the inside. Even though her pain was unbearable, yet she 
refused to call a physician out of bashfulness and to give the others an example 
of the highest level of faith amid the suffering and of perseverance amid the 
temptation. However, God's compassion to those like this saint is so exalted to 
realize the marvel ous promise: “ Though he falls, he shall not be utterly cast 
down; for the Lord upholds him with His hand .” (Ps. 37:24) . Gorgonia's 
healing was as elevated as her calamity was intense.” 
Healing from a Serious Illness: 
According to her brother St. Gregory th e Nazianzus:  “She once was 
inflicted by a wicked illness that caused intense fever to all her being . She 
would feel her blood boiling in her veins, and have partial mental paralysis and 
severe pain in her extremities . Her physicians stood helpless, and the tears of 
her family and supplications of those around her were to no avail . Now, what 
did that great soul do, whose well-being meant the well-being of her beloved, 
and her sufferings and illness meant a general calamity? 
She resorted to the Higher Physician, followed the lead of the woman with 
the flow of blood who touched the hem of the robe of Christ (Matt. 9:20). She 
approached the temple with hope, cried out loudly calling her Awesome God, 
recalling His past exalted deeds with her, shed a flow of tears like the woman 
who wetted His feet with her tears (Luke 7:38), then had communion from the 
holy body and precious blood of the Lord. Amazingly, she felt on the spot that 
her body, soul, and spirit were utterly healed. Because of her spiritual strength, 
and holding fast to hope, she got physical strength. 
Yes, those things may look amazing, but believe me, they are a fact I 
revealed to you because she kept silent about them during her life. I find it my 
duty to explain it so that such a beautiful miracle would not remain secret.”

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 1, p. 212
passages.text:
212 
 
twelfth regiment ‘The Regiment of Thunder, ’ because, by their prayers, the 
miracle happened. He also issued a decree in which he wrote that his army was 
on the brink of destruction by thirst in Germany but was saved by the prayers 
of the Christian soldiers, and threatened death against anyone saying 
otherwise. This saint, most probably, reposed in the Lord in the year 179 AD 
and is celebrated by the Western Church on the 8th of January. 
 [Eusebius: Hist. Eccl. 4:27; 5:5]  
 
APOLLINARIUS, BISHOP OF RAVENNA 
According to the ‘Catholic’ Church, he was the first bishop in the city of 
‘Ravenna’ in Italy. He was sent there by St. Peter, the apostle. He was born in 
Antioch. On his way to Ravenna, a blind boy asked him for a donation; so, he 
prayed for him, and Jesus Christ restored his sight. A multitude of people 
gathered around him, and he preached t hem about the Savior. The boy, his 
father ‘Erinaius’ and his whole family, proclaimed their faith in the Lord 
Christ. 
The news spread and a leader in the army sought from him to heal his wife 
who was on the brink of death. He prayed for her, made the sign of the cross 
on her, and she was instantly healed. The house of the leader turned into a 
church in which the believers gathered on a regular basis. 
The Pagans turned Against Him: 
The pagan priests, feeling that their status was threatened because many of 
their people turned into Christianity, they complained to the governor of the 
city. The governor called the saint and asked him: “Why do you oppose the 
god, Jupiter?” The saint answered him: “I do not know a god by this name. ” 
Then, the governor took him to  the temple and showed him the greatness of 
what was in it. The saint then, cried, saying: “Do you worship your handiwork 
and offer to the silver and gold the worship befitting to God alone, the Creator 
of heavens and earth? Hearing this, the pagans were s tirred up against him, 
struck him with a rod, and stoned him until they thought he was dead. They 
dragged him outside the city and left him there. The believers came and found 
him still alive; they carried him to a house in the city and cared for him until  
he regained his strength. Then, he got up and started to preach them as he used 
to do. 
In the House of the Noble ‘Boniface’: 
A nobleman in the city called ‘Boniface,’ he was mute, and the physicians 
in town could not help him. So, he sent his wife to seek from the saint to come 
over to heal him. The saint went along with her, and in their house, he found a

passages.label: Encyclopedia of the Saints and Fathers of the Church, Volume 4, p. 158
passages.text:
158 
 
climb up on it. Once he did reach up to him, he showed him his wounded legs, 
to assure him about his human nature. 
An Exalted Fatherhood: 
Along with his firmness and cruelty on himself, the saint was so 
compassionate, meek, and cheerful toward all others. The two sermons he gave 
every day raised the hearts of his listeners to heaven. He gave them a chance 
to ask questions. And, he used to reconcile the adversaries. Together with his 
love, he never complimented  anyone at the expense of his salvation.  He 
counseled the kings and the elites and cared for the Church leaderships. 
A Heavenly Message: 
In a night vision, he felt that someone was calling his name. He instantly 
woke up, to see a person of heavenly beauty, clothed with splendid light and 
holding a golden rod in his hand. Then for his fear, he fell on the ground, but 
the angel gave him peace and said to him: “Do not be afraid; follow me and 
listen carefully to what I am about to say: The Lord is planning to use you for 
the glory of His Name, for t he improvement of His Church and to bring back 
so many people from their sinful ways. But, you have to know that you are 
committed to suffer much. And you have to condition your heart into complete 
perseverance and love for all men regardless of their char acters. And above 
everything else, you have to take away from your mind every thought of pride 
or vainglory; and to put yourself in a level lower than any other man in the 
world.” The angel then brought him forth to the top of the mountain, instructed 
him to build an altar using four rocks. Then, he took him over to a Church, 
where he saw a crowd of people from all races in heavenly attire, with the 
portrait of humility and piety on their faces. And, the angel told him that these 
were the people who returned to God, because of his sermons and by following 
his role model. 
Entering into the Church and approaching the altar to pray, he saw the Lord 
Christ, more splendid than the sun. The Lord Jesus greeted him and said: “Have 
courage and never fear.” 
A Heavenly Support: 
In another night's vision, he saw Elijah the prophet on a fiery chariot. Elijah 
counseled him to have no fear before the elites of the world, for as long as God 
would be his support, no one could ever harm him. 
His Humility: 
As some recluses developed some doubts concerning the saint's strange way 
of worship, dwelling on a pillar, his long prayers and continuous sermons to

their assignment, they went back, each to his ministry. 
Out of compassion on his people, St. Germanus sought from the governor 
of the city – whose wife he healed earlier – to reduce their taxes , and the 
governor did according to his request. 
In the year 440 AD, the heresy of Pelagius reappeared in Britain, and the 
saint was asked to go back again . When he did, he managed to put an end to 
the heresy and the heretics by his sound teaching and by performing miracles, 
and he brought them back to the upright faith . Realizing that England needed 
well-educated clergy to hold faith f ast and to overcome ignorance in the face 
of the heretic teachings , the saint established religious schools to teach them 
the sound doctrine. 
His Miracles: 
Because of his love for God and his people, God granted him the grace to 
perform signs and miracles wherever he went. During his first visit to Britain, 
the land was threatened by an invasion from the enemies . The people asked 
him to pray for them and give them his blessings, which he did . He used the 
chance to call the non-believers among the army to Ch ristianity, and many of 
them were baptized. They built a church in which they celebrated the feast of 
Resurrection. After the feast, in an attempt to save them from having their 
bloodshed, he let the army go between two high mountains and instructed them 
at his sign to shout with a thunderous voice: Alleluia, which would be further 
magnified by the echo . Hearing it, the enemy assumed that they were 
surrounded by a great army, and they discarded their weapons and fled away. 
A messenger from Britain came to him to ask bishop Germanus in the name 
of the people for him to intercede for them before the emperor because they 
revolted against him, and he was sending his very violent deputy Isius with his 
forces to take revenge.  
The bishop did not hesitate to travel  to meet with the deputy who was on 
his way to do his job. The saint asked him to have compassion for those people, 
to which he utterly refused . The bishop took hold of the harness of his wild 
horse and calmed it down . Astonished at the courage of the old er man, the 
commander promised to put his mission on hold, until the bishop would go to 
the emperor to get his permission to forgive those people.  
Going to Italy to plead his case, the bishop spent the night in the house of a 
priest who was his friend. There he anointed his mute daughter with the holy 
oil, prayed for her, and she was healed.  
In the way, he encountered an older man carrying a heavy burden and was 
trying to cross a canal . The saint took the load off him, carried it a cross the 
canal, then returned to carry the older man himself and crossed the canal again. 
The saint did all that although he was as old and frail because of his asceticism.

His Strife: 
He loved the life of seclusion and tranquility under the guidance of his 
mentor abba ‘Paul,’ practicing a severely ascetic life in his  attire, fasting,

God’s Wonders through Him: 
A disabled man, since his birth, kept on visiting the monastery. Then, he 
heard about the holy pious life of St. ‘Badasuis.' So, he asked him to pray for 
him and make the sign of the Cross on him. When the saint did that, the 
disabled man was healed, and he jumped joyfully praising God. The same 
miracle happened with a blind man, and the fame of St. ‘Badasius’ spread so 
fast that a multitude of people came seeking his prayers and blessings in the 
Lord. 
On seeing the work of God through him, the abbot of the monastery decided 
to let him wear the holy monastic ‘Eskeem’ (which is given to the monks of 
high spiritual stature). On hearing of that plan, St. ‘Badasuis’ secretly fled the

embittered because of that city having no shepherd, so he stood up before God, 
crying out with tears on being unable to put his hands on G regory to ordain 
him a bishop. He kept praying and asking God to resolve that problem. When

His Pastoral Work and Wonders: 
Once the saint was walking along the streets of the city , and he found a 
temple for the idols, so he entered into it. The saint prayed there for the whole 
night and left. When the priest of the pagan temple came in the morning, he 
found out that the demons residing there have disappeared. So, he went to the 
governor of the city and filed a complaint that a Christian entered into the 
temple and drove the demons away from it. On hearing about that, St. Gregory 
went to the priest and talked to him about the True God and explaine d to him 
the facts of faith, but the priest requested him to bring his gods the demons 
back. The Saint wrote a note on a piece of paper, saying: “From Gregorius to 
the devil, I tell you: to come back.” The pagan priest carried that piece of paper 
to the altar, and the demons came back . Then, the priest realized how lowly 
those evil spirits were, and he set forth to the saint, seeking to introduce him 
to the truth. The saint preached the Gospel and the C hristian teaching to him 
and confirmed it, in the name of Christ, by ordering a rock lodged in front of 
them to move, and it did obey him. 
On hearing about that, many of the pagans in the city came out to welcome 
the saint and to seek from him to preach them. Within a short time, through his 
sermons, his holy life in the Lord , and the amazing works of God upon his 
hands, many of them proclaimed their faith in the Lord . St. Gregory of Nyssa 
has given an account about some of those amazing works of God which took 
place through this saint, and St. Basil the Great has said about him: “Through 
the work of the Spirit, Gregory had the authority on the evil spirits , diverted 
the course of some rivers in the name of Christ, dried up a lake that was the 
cause of contr oversy between two brothers , and prophesized about things to 
come. Those signs and wonders were seen by both the friends and enemies of 
the truth, as though he was another Moses.” St. Gregory of Nyssa said: “As it 
is impossible of us to mention all the wonders of that saint, it is enough to say 
that by one word and by the sign of the Holy Cross, he healed multitudes of 
the sick. Therefore, he was counted as a saint by all.” 
It was said that two of the Jews planned to tarnish the saint's reputation as a 
wonder-maker, as well as, to rob him of some money . So, one of them 
pretended to be dead, while the other requested money from him to shroud his 
friend. Having nothing with him, the saint gave him his robe. The young man

Once, a hyena came to  his cell and attempted to drag him by his robe . He 
followed it to its cave, where it brought its three handicapped cubs to the 
saint. Amazed at the wisdom of that beast, he prayed, put his hand on the 
three cubs, healed them, and went his way to his cell. After a while, the hyena 
came back holding by its mouth a piece of leather hide, which the saint kept 
using as a floor-mat until the day he reposed. 
When it happened that there was no rain in Alexandria for an extended 
period, he was called over by the pope. Once he reached the papal residence, 
the rain started pouring and kept on until they sought from the saint to stop it . 
He then prayed, and it did. 
Healing a Priest from Cancer: 
Once, a priest who was inflicted with Cancer which caused the bones of 
his face to be exposed and made him look e xtremely horrible; came to St. 
Macarius, and cast himself down at his feet, asking him to pray on his behalf, 
but the saint turned his face away from him . Those present implored the 
saint, saying: “Father, have mercy on the man, look at him and respond to his 
request.” The saint answered them, saying: “Leave him alone, he does not 
deserve to be healed, for he enters into the Holy Place of Sacrifice while he is 
defiled.” The priest kept begging the saint for three days until he finally had 
compassion upon his tears. The saint called him and said: “Do you know why 
God brought this punishment on you?” The priest answered him : “Yes, I do, 
father.” The saint said: “As long as you perceive your sins, then repent to be 
saved,” and he sought from the man to forsake his priesthood work to be 
saved from the eternal torment . When the man promised that he would do 
that, the saint anointed his face and head with holy oil, and God healed him . 
The man then sought permission to go, saying: “I shall stay among the people 
as a layman until the day I die.” 
His Cell was Robbed: 
When a famine dwelt on the land, some Libyan thieves wandering in the 
desert came to the saint's cell, while he was not there. They took all his hand-
work made of p alm leaves, and the vessels he used to give hospitality to his 
guests. When they were about to go their way, their camel could not stand up 
on its feet and kept moaning until the morning.  
Abba Macarius in his way back to his cell, saw them and he assumed that 
they came to provide him with the needs of the monks , but soon he realized 
that they were thieves. They prostrated themselves to the ground before him, 
and he did not get angry, but entered into his cell and brought them a vessel 
of pickled olives, wh ich they missed because it was hidden behind the door . 
He said to them: “Do you want to know why your camel could not get up?”

records.answer:
I could not find anything about filioque in the loaded sources.

The passages do cover topics related to the Council of Chalcedon, Christology, and relations between the Coptic Orthodox Church and the Roman Catholic Church, including some historical interactions and theological dialogues [9][10][11][12][14][16]. However, none mention the filioque or explicitly compare the Coptic and Catholic positions on it. 

| Aspect                          | Coptic Orthodox Church Position                         | Roman Catholic Church Position                       |
|--------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| Filioque                       | Not described in the sources.                           | Not described in the sources.                       |
| Christology and Council of Chalcedon | Rejects the Chalcedonian formula "in two natures" as it is seen as not assuring hypostatic unity; adheres to the Cyrillian formula "one incarnate nature of God the Word" [11][12][16]. | Accepts the Chalcedonian definition and the Tome of Leo, which uses the formula "in two natures" [11][12]. |
| Relations and Dialogue          | Has engaged in dialogue with Chalcedonian Orthodox and Catholic Churches, clarifying misunderstandings and affirming orthodoxy [9][10][14]. | Engaged in dialogue with the Coptic Church; some Catholics have tried to bring Copts into communion [10][14]. |
| Liturgical Tradition            | Retains ancient liturgical forms dating back to the 5th century, with specific Coptic liturgies [17]. | Not described in the sources.                       |

Book 1: Introduction to the Coptic Catechism 
13 
persons were not united essentially or hypostatically, but merely morally or in character. 
Thus, Christ is not to be called God but “Theophorus” or “God-bearer,” just as we would call 
the saints because of the work of divine grace in them. As a result, Mary is not the mother of 
God, but the mother of the human Jesus in whom the divinity dwelt. Nestorius and his 
followers criticized the Magi for their worship of the Child Jesus and held that His divinity 
was parted from Him at the moment of crucifixion. 
What impact did the three Councils have on the Catechism of the Christian Sees or 
the Universal Church? 
All the apostolic Churches — whether Orthodox Chalcedonians, non -Chalcedonians or 
the Roman Catholic Church — consider these three ecumenical councils as being responsible 
for clarifying the faith, especially with regard to the Holy Trinity; and for the defense against 
many of the heresies that appeared in this period. Although there were some small disputes 
over the language of some expressions, these councils carried on their discussions in a spirit 
of love and holy zeal for the faith. 
As for the Council of Chalcedon in the year 451 A. D., some apostolic Churches hold 
that it did not introduce anything new, but only explained and clarified the first three 
ecumenical councils. Our unofficial and official dialogues with the apostolic Chalcedonian 
Orthodox Churches and the Catholic Church in the late twentieth century brought more 
openness. All of them came to realize that we are not Eutychians as they had thought; that is, 
we do not proclaim that His humanity was annihilated within His divinity.  
Thus, we achieved positive results together with our Orthodox Chalcedonian brethren. 
I recall, for example, that in the first official meeting between the two families, the 
Chalcedonians refused to call us “Orthodox,” insisting instead on referring to us as the 
“Ancient Eastern Churches.” After discussions filled with love, the following occurred: 
First: After many years of dialo gue with a Greek theologian, I asked him: “Do you 
remember the day when you refused to call us Orthodox?” He smiled and said: “We feel a 
sense of unity with you, perhaps even more than that which we feel among ourselves, 
between Orthodox Chalcedonians.” 
Second: A well -known priest and dear friend took the initiative of supervising the 
doctoral thesis for some of Copts in England. He would answer every person who accused 
St. Dioscorus with heresy by saying: “I have the proceedings of the Council of Chalcedon in 
the Greek language. They witness to the fact that this St. Dioscorus was not accused of 
heresy, but of insulting the Pope of Rome.”  
Third: When the two Orthodox families opened up in the spirit of mutual love, whenever 
this father would walk by, some Chalcedonians would whisper to one another that the 
defender of the Coptic Church had come.

Consequently, a high religious court was held, attended by the Muslim sheiks 
in Egypt, the head of the Coptic church, and representatives of the Roman 
church. The high religious court issued a decision and was del ivered to the 
pope. The decision could be summarized as follows: “Whoever of the Copts 
changes his sect, and joins the foreign sect, should accordingly be punished by 
the officials, to make him an example to others.” 
In the year 1741 AD, the Roman Pope Ben edict XIV (1740 -1758 AD), 
ordained a ‘Coptic/Catholic’ priest in Jerusalem by the name of Athanasius, as 
a metropolitan on Egypt. Yet he did not come to Egypt, but spent the rest of 
his life in Jerusalem, leaving his deputy in Egypt, to a priest called Jus tus el-
Maraghy to represent him there. 
Among the most well-known personalities which the Catholics managed to 
lure them to their camp by the end of the 18 th century AD, was a young Copt 
called Raphael el-Tukhi of Girga. The Catholics took him while he was still a 
child, and sent him to Rome to study theology. Then, after he graduated, he 
was ordained by the Roman pope as a bishop on Arsinoe (Fayyum). However, 
he was excommunicated by the Coptic church and was opposed by the local 
authorities. Eventually, he was called back to Rome to help writing books in 
the Coptic language and to revise the books on the rites of the church. He lived 
in Rome until his death. 
The Coptic Pope John XVII, striving to keep his children in the fold of their 
mother Orthodox church, made a pastoral trip to the cities where the Catholics 
set their centers. There, he supported his priests, gave sermons to his people, 
and unceasingly send them messages and books he wrote, to urge them to be 
aware not to be seduced or to be diverted awa y from their faith; and to hold 
fast to that faith delivered to us by the saints. In all his writings, he concentrated 
on the following: 
 Our church is the church of the martyrs who shed their blood to keep the 
upright faith. 
 As long as Emanuel, our God is on our side; we have more on our team than 
those against us. 
 The tribulations could never be compared to the glory to come. 
 The tribulations are the way to enter into the heavenly glories. 
 These tribulations are only physical and temporary: “He who endures to the 
end shall be saved.” (Matthew 24:13). 
This great pope succeeded, to a great extent, and by the grace of the Holy 
Spirit, in keeping Coptic heritage, we received from our fathers. Among the 
essential manuscripts, this pope left to his church is the Psalms of the Agpeya, 
the Ten Commandments; the Seven Holy Sacraments; and the Evangelic 
advice.

New Testament and so he chanted saying, “this is none other them the house of God and 
this is the gate of heaven” (Gen. 28:17). 
Second: The era of the Mosaic Law and Prophets: The law explained in detail the 
sacrifices and their rituals as a symbol of Christ’s sacrifice. The prophets wro te many 
prophecies about the Savior, His birth, crucifixion, burial, resurrection, and ascension.  
Third: The era of the incarnation of the Logos until His ascension: The Lord revealed 
His divine love to us, so He fed the hungry, healed the sick, comforted the brokenhearted and 
revealed to them His providence even after His ascension when He sent them the Comforter, 
the Holy Spirit. He announced to them the Father’s love to all humanity and the Holy Spirit’s 
work to declare the divine truth and lead the Church to heaven as she struggles in the world.  
Fourth: The era between Christ’s ascension until His second coming: Here, He acts 
as a heavenly high priest. The Apostle Paul spoke about this era in his epistle to the Hebrews 
(Heb. 6:20) in which he compares between the high priests who were in need of redemption 
and the unique heavenly High Priest.  
453. Why does the Creed mention the Church after talking about the oneness of God 
and the Holy Trinity? 
The goal of the Orthodox Creed is not to mention some theoretical facts about God, the 
world, the Church, the final judgment, and the eternal life, but its main goal is to help the 
believer encounter God, enjoy His love as he struggles in the world, prepare him for the great 
day of the Lord, help him have com munion with the heavenly, and have eternal life. So, as 
we confess our faith saying, “ and in One Holy Catholic and Apostolic Church,” we are 
affirming our commitment to be in communion with the Holy God, to love one another, to 
have a relationship with our  friends in heaven as we join their praising choir and enjoy our 
sonship to God on an eternal level.  
Our knowledge of the Church drives us to look forward to our life in heaven when we 
depart and meet the heavenly Bridegroom who will welcome us in a joyfu l heavenly 
procession which the heavenly hosts look forward to saying, “thrust in your sickle and reap” 
(Rev. 14:15). We should not marvel that the heavenly hosts are earnestly looking forward to 
the day of the Lord, since they view our Church not as a social institution governed by some 
laws that are in place to ensure man’s happiness, but as the people of God who are being 
prepared to partake in the angelic life where the believer experiences God’s plan for him 
every day. Therefore, we should not be surprised if we hear about many of the saints such as 
St. John Chrysostom who felt that they were the happiest people in the world. The believer 
has his eyes fixed on his Creator and Savior and what He is preparing for him in heaven, so 
he is joyful in the midst of his hardships. The believer performs his job with all honesty and 
is faithful in his relationships with others, because he considers himself to be a child of God 
who does not know failure, despair, or greed as he is the ambassador of heaven on earth.

Some scholars have been in the habit of attributing violence to the Alexandrian fathers 
and theologians, even to Athanasius and Cyril. 
St. Dioscorus and the Council of Chalcedon: although the Council of Chalcedon was 
thought to have been convened to try Eutyches, in the event, its attention turned to attacking 
Pope Dioscorus of Alexandria, rather than the old monk. Eutyches was not even present at 
the council, having been exiled to north Syria before the council met.  
In fact, Dioscor us was condemned not because of any theological heresy, but due to 
political circumstances which dominated this council.  
The Greek Professor Fr. Romanides says, “Dioscorus was considered quite orthodox 
in his faith by such leading Fathers of the Council of Chalcedon as those represented 
by Anatolius of Constantinople.” 19 Metropolitan Methodios of Aksum also says, 
“Information, which we possess, does not depict Dioscorus as a heretic. From available 
information it is obvious that he was a good man and even Bishop Leo himself tried to take 
him to his side … Likewise Emperor Theodosius in a letter to Dioscorus calls him a man 
who radiates the Grace of God, a humble man and of orthodox faith. 
“Several times in the course of the Council Patriarch Diosco rus declared his faith. He 
was not condemned because he was heretical but because he refused to communicate with 
Leo, the Archbishop, and because he refused to come to the Council although he was invited 
to do so three times. 
“This evidence is sufficient for us to look for other reasons for Dioscorus’ condemnation. 
Rome was annoyed by the extraordinary vitality of the Church of Alexandria and its active 
Patriarch.”20  
The emperor accepted the council’s decision and exiled Pope Dioscorus to the island of 
Gangra in Asia Minor. He remained in exile for five years, occupying his time in guiding the 
lost and healing the sick. He departed to the glorious realm in the year 457 A. D. 
What impact did the Council of Chalcedon have on the catechism of the Church?  
a. The rise of strong theologians, such as Philoxenus of Mabbug, Pope Timothy, and the 
great teacher St. Severus of Antioch, who preserved the orthodoxy of the faith. Fr.

On the Main Features of the Coptic Liturgy 
790. What are the features of Egyptian liturgy? 
The East in general, and Egyptian Church in particular, still retains the spirit of the 
apostolic patristic Liturgy. The liturgical texts that are used have not changed very much 
since the fifth century, which gives the study of the Egyptian liturgy particular importance. 
In his book “The Early Liturgy,” Father Jungmann says, “especially in the general structure 
of the Mass, the Oriental rites have kept many primitive characteristics which have 
disappeared from the Roman rite … Whereas our Mass changes day after day, the Orient 
constantly repeats the same invariable formulary.”1546 Fr. Dix, the Anglican monk, says, “The 
main lines of all the Eastern traditions had been reached before the end of the fourth century, 
and after this the process in all of them is no more than one of adjustment and developmen t 
of detail. No new principle arose in the fifth century, as it did in the West …” 1547 
791. Which eucharistic Liturgies does the Coptic Church currently use? 
a. The Liturgy of St. Basil the Great. The Coptic Liturgy differs from the Byzantine 
Liturgy of the same name. This Liturgy is the one that is most often used.  
b. The Liturgy of St. Gregory the Theologian.  Often used on special occasions and 
feasts. Prayers of this Liturgy address the hypostasis of the Son. It is not unique in 
doing so because there are other liturgies with the same style, such as other Egyptian 
liturgies, three Ethiopian liturgies, the Syrian Liturgy of Saints Addai and Mari, and 
the Syrian Liturgy of St. Jacob. 
c. The Liturgy of St. Cyril (St. Mark the Evangelist).  St. Cyril of Alexandria 
compiled it and edited the older Liturgy of St. Mark; so it came to be named after 
him. Its use is less widespread than the previous two. 
792. What are the main sections of the Coptic Liturgy? 
The Liturgy can be divided into three services:  
a. Offering of the Lamb. The Lamb is chosen from among the offered loaves of bread.

Lamb was once part of the Liturgy of the Faithful, but just before the fifth century, 
this rite was moved to the begin ning of the Liturgy instead, in order to prepare the 
congregation for the renewal of their covenant with God by listening to God’s word 
and partaking of the sacraments. It is the beginning of the journey where the Church

records.question: Give me a bullet list of what the Coptic Church teaches about the Immaculate Conception
records.answer:
I could not find anything about Immaculate Conception in the loaded sources.

The passages do cover several teachings about the Virgin Mary, including:

- The Coptic Church celebrates several feasts of the Theotokos (Mother of God), such as the annunciation of her birth, her birthday, her entry into the temple, her departure, the revealing of the assumption of her body, the consecration of the first church in her name, and the apparition of the Virgin Mary above her church in Zeitoun [1].
- The Son of God took a body from the womb of the Virgin Mary and became a human being without ceasing to be God; He became a fetus without sin [2].
- At the annunciation of the incarnation, the angel Gabriel said, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Highest will overshadow you” (Luke 1:35), indicating the miraculous conception of Jesus in the Virgin Mary [2].
- The Coptic Church uses the term “Theotokos” to describe St. Mary, a term beloved in Coptic texts in every age [5].
- The Virgin Mary is seen as the living ark of the covenant, the dwelling of the Most High, and the second heaven [1].
- The Church honors Mary on her birthday as a joyful day, unlike other saints who are commemorated on their departure day [1].

These points relate to the Virgin Mary and the incarnation but do not specifically address the doctrine of the Immaculate Conception.

1084. What are the feasts of the Theotokos, the Mother of God? 
In addition to the monthly commemoration of the Virgin Mary on the 21 st of every 
Coptic month, we celebrate the following feasts: 
a. The annunciation of her birth (7th Mesore / 13 th August). On this feast we 
celebrate the conception of St. Mary, the living ark of the covenant, the dwelling of 
the Most High, and the second heaven. 
b. Her birthday (1st Pashons / 9th May). Copts usually commemorate the day a saint 
passed from this world; their  martyrdom or departure to paradise  — but they insist 
on honoring St. Mary on her the day of her birth as a joyful day.  
c. Her entry into the temple (3rd Kiahk / 12 th December). We learn from the 
tradition of the Church that St. Mary’s life was consecrated to God in fulfillment of 
her mother’s vow, for she had vowed to consecrate her firstborn — whether a son or 
a daughter — to serve the Lord all the days of his or her life. 
d. Her departure (21st Tobe / 29th January).

feast is preceded by the fifteen-day fast of St. Mary.

melting iron in the city of Bartus.

‘The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Highest will oversh adow you; 
therefore, also, that Holy One who is to be born will be called the Son of God.’” (Luke 1:34–
35).  
121. What does the phrase “was incarnate and became man” mean?  
The Son of God took for Himself a body from the womb of the Virgin, St. Mary and 
became a fetus without sin. He became a human being without ceasing being God. The 
evangelist says, “and the Word became flesh” (John 1:14). This God who became man 
intercedes for all humanity, offering Himself as a sacrifice for their sake. Therefore, the 
apostle Paul affirms that He became a man in truth, and not just as the illusion of a body, as 
the Gnostics claimed. He said, “For there is one God and one Mediator between God and 
men, the Man Christ Jesus” (1 Tim. 2:5).  
122. How is there only one nature in Christ?  
In Christ there is one nature of two natures, without mingling, without confusion, and 
without alteration. This is the nature of the Word who became Man. The Church equally 
rejects the Nestorian concept of Christ being two persons , and the faith of Eutyc hes who 
proclaimed that His humanity was swallowed up by His divinity or was dissolved in it.  
Through the unofficial and official dialogues between the Chalcedonian Orthodox and 
the non-Chalcedonian Orthodox, both affirmed their rejection of both the Nest orian and the 
Eutychian understandings. Further, both families asserted their rejection of any division or 
confusion between His divinity and His humanity.  
123. Why does the Creed include the phrase, “was incarnate of the Holy Spirit and of 
the Virgin Mary”? 
The history of the people of God is marked by a number of miraculous births, such as: 
God’s promise to Abraham and Sarah of the birth of Isaac (Gen. 17:16–19); Hannah and the 
birth of Samuel the prophet (1 Sam. 1:1 –20); Manoah and his barren wife and the bi rth of 
their son Samson (Judg. 13:2–3); and Zacharias the priest and Elizabeth and the birth of John 
the Baptist (Luke 1:5–25). But a young, unknown virgin conceiving and bringing forth Jesus 
the Savior of the world surpassed all previous divine promises; for the Virgin bore in her 
body the promise of the salvation of the world. At the annunciation of the incarnation, the 
angel Gabriel said, “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Highest will 
overshadow you” (Luke 1:35).  
The existence of polytheism in the world cried out for the Son to come, as St. Cyril of 
Jerusalem explains: “Was it without reason that the Son came? or was it in order that the 
Father might be acknowledged? You have learned what moved the Only -begotten to come 
down from the throne at God’s right hand. The Father was despised, the Son must needs

7 
1 
(b) The Coptic Catechism Through the Ages 
3. How did the Church preserve the correct faith through the ages? 
I greatly desired to present a Coptic Orthodox Catechism to reveal our Christian 
understanding concisely and briefly; particularly because, due to ecclesiastical and political 
circumstances, our Church was isolated from Western churches in the fifth century A. D. and 
remained so to a large extent up until the twentieth century, when she was accused by many 
in the West of adhering to Eutychianism. The Coptic Church, therefore, did not have the 
opportunity to reveal her true teachings through the writings of her Fathers and her liturgies. 
Despite the Church’s participation in many international theological conferences in recent 
years, insisting upon her rejection of Eutychianism, some sources continue to at tribute this 
heresy to our Church, of which the Church is completely innocent and strongly opposes 
through her liturgies and praises. 
In a certain dialogue with the Chalcedonian Orthodox Churches, theologians were 
surprised to observe that the liturgies an d praises that we enjoy to the present day lack even 
the slightest hint of Eutychianism, but rather, positively oppose it in a beautifully Christian 
manner; especially the daily Theotokias and those of the festal celebrations. Some of the 
theologians observed that they harmonize with the thought St. Cyril, or that perhaps he was 
their author.  
A Greek theologian once asked me whether we use the word “Theotokos” to describe St. 
Mary and was astonished to learn that it is a term beloved in Coptic texts in every age.  
4. What are the stages of development of Coptic Catechism through the ages? 
It is worth laying out the circumstances through which the Coptic Church has endured, 
from her foundation till the present day, that we may grasp the truth of her teachings, and 
benefit from her long experience over twenty centuries. 
Our Coptic Church has continuously faced persecution since the middle of the first 
century and until the present time. Thus, Mrs. Butcher, a Professor of History at Oxford 
University, expressed her amazement when she stated that the endurance of the Copts to this 
day is one of the wonders of the world. 
In the eighth century B. C., Isaiah the prophet anticipated the Coptic Church and wrote 
with the spirit of prophecy of her marvelous beginnings.  
The Church suffered many persecutions, even from fellow Christians. Such were the 
persecutions by the Emperors of Constantinople who persecuted her and appointed patriarchs
